desc: It possesses bimodal molecular weight distribution, which improves processability. This grade meets
the requirements of material as per clause 5.2 of IS 4984:2016 for 'Polyethylene pipes for Water
Supply - Specification'. When incorporated with adequate quantity of carbon black masterbatch as
specified in clause 5.3 of IS: 4984: 2016, pipes made with this grade confirms to all specifications as
Pipe made from Relene 45GP004 grade passes the Internal Pressure Creep Rupture Test when
tested with 4.5 MPa induced stress at 80°C for 165 hrs and with 4.9 MPa induced stress at 80°C for
48 hrs as per clause 8.1 of IS 4984:2016, thereby meeting the requirement of PE:80 grade.

competition.key_props: 1. MRS >8 MPa 2. Hydrostatic Pressure >1000 hrs @ 80°C/4.0 MPa 3. ESCR >1000 Hrs, OIT >30 Min
competition.superior: Meets PE80 standard with bimodal molecular weight distribution for improved processability and excellent long-term hydrostatic strength.
competition.limitations: Lower MRS classification (PE80 vs PE100), not suitable for high-pressure applications requiring PE100 rating
competition.comparison: 1. Reliance offers higher ESCR (>1000 Hrs) and higher tensile strength (27 MPa vs 25 MPa for Haldia) 2. while Haldia P5100 offers higher flexural modulus (1000 MPa vs 850 MPa for Reliance) and better processability
competition.reason_haldia_better: Haldia P5100 combines excellent processability with good creep resistance, ESCR, and mechanical properties, offering higher stiffness (Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa) for pressure pipe applications.

desc: It possesses bimodal molecular weight distribution which improves processability. This grade meets

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/5 kg) 0.30 g/10 min 2. Density 0.948 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 28 MPa 4. Flexural Modulus 850 MPa 5. Notched Izod Impact No Break 6. ESCR (F50) >1000 hrs 7. OIT @200°C >30 min
competition.superior: Bimodal MWD PE100 grade; passes IS 4984:2016 creep rupture at 5.4 MPa @ 80°C / 165 hrs, qualifying full PE100 pressure class.
competition.limitations: 1. Low MFI (0.30 g/10 min @ 5 kg) demands high-torque pipe extruders and careful die design 2. Supplied natural — requires carbon black masterbatch per clause 5.3 of IS 4984:2016 for finished black pipe 3. Not optimised for non-pressure duct or trenchless installation
competition.comparison: 1. Both are PE100 grades — Haldia P5300 is certified MRS 10 MPa per ISO 9080 and designated PE 100 per ISO 12162 2. Haldia P5300 offers higher stiffness (Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa vs 850 MPa) and higher tensile strength @ break (40 MPa vs Not available in official TDS) 3. Both carry ESCR >1000 hrs and OIT >30 min
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia P5300 carries a declared RCP critical pressure ≥10 Bar (ISO 13477) — a rapid-crack-propagation figure Reliance 46GP003 does not state — which is the governing property for large-diameter, high-pressure gas and water mains 2. Its 270 J/m notched Izod and 1000 MPa flexural modulus give better resistance to installation impact damage in rocky trenches 3. Trade-off: P5300's much lower MFI (0.25 g/10 min @ 5 kg vs 0.30) raises extruder load, so 46GP003 is the easier grade to run on older, lower-torque pipe lines

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/5 kg) 0.9 g/10 min 2. Density 0.948 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 24.0 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 11.0% 5. Elongation @ Break >600% 6. ESCR (F50) >1000 hrs
competition.superior: Bimodal MWD PE63 grade with dual capability — qualifies for both pressure pipe under IS 4984:2016 and pesticide bottle blow moulding.
competition.limitations: 1. PE63 classification — not suitable for PE80 or PE100 pressure duty 2. Flexural Modulus Not available in official TDS, limiting stiffness-driven design calculations 3. Requires carbon black masterbatch for finished black pipe
competition.comparison: 1. Both are PE63-compliant pressure pipe grades 2. Haldia P5200 runs at much lower MFI (0.90 g/10 min @ 5 kg vs 0.9 for Reliance — comparable) with declared Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa, which 46GP009 does not state 3. Both carry ESCR >1000 hrs; P5200 declares Notched Izod 175 J/m and Tensile Strength @ Break 38 MPa
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia P5200 publishes a complete mechanical dataset (Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa, Izod 175 J/m, TS @ Break 38 MPa, Vicat 123 °C) that lets a designer verify SDR and ring stiffness — figures absent from the 46GP009 TDS 2. Trade-off: P5200 is a dedicated pipe grade only. Reliance 46GP009 is dual-purpose and is the better choice where one resin must serve both PE63 pipe and pesticide bottle blow moulding, since Haldia has no equivalent dual-claim grade

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/5 kg) 0.9 g/10 min 2. Density 0.948 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 24.0 MPa 4. Flexural Modulus 750 MPa 5. ESCR (F50) >1000 hrs 6. HDT 72 °C 7. OIT @200°C >30 min 8. Hardness Shore D 63
competition.superior: UV-stabilised bimodal formulation designed to sustain outdoor exposure for telecom duct service life.
competition.limitations: 1. Optimised for ducts — not intended for PE80/PE100 pressure pipe 2. Lower flexural modulus (750 MPa) than dedicated pipe grades, limiting ring stiffness in thin-wall duct 3. Notched Izod Impact Not available in official TDS
competition.comparison: 1. Both are UV-stabilised HDPE telecom duct grades with ESCR >1000 hrs 2. Haldia P5200UV offers substantially higher stiffness (Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa vs 750 MPa) and declares Notched Izod 175 J/m, which 46GP009UV does not state 3. Haldia P5200UV has higher Vicat Softening Point (125 °C vs HDT 72 °C reported for Reliance — different test basis, not directly comparable)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia P5200UV is stabilised with HALS+ specifically for long outdoor service life, and its 1000 MPa flexural modulus vs 750 MPa gives materially better duct ring stiffness — the property that resists crushing during ploughing-in and back-fill 2. Declared Izod of 175 J/m provides a verifiable impact figure for cold-weather duct installation, which the Reliance TDS omits 3. Trade-off: the two are otherwise closely matched on ESCR and density, so the choice is driven by duct wall thickness and installation method rather than resin chemistry

competition.limitations: 1. Very low MFI (0.26 g/10 min @ 5 kg) requires accumulator-head machines — not suitable for small or thin-wall containers 2. ESCR Not available in official TDS 3. Supplied without UV stabiliser — external UV masterbatch needed for outdoor tanks
competition.comparison: 1. Both are HMHDPE large-part blow moulding grades with comparable flow (MFI5 0.35 for B5500 vs 0.26 for Reliance) 2. Reliance 52GB002 offers higher flexural modulus (1050 MPa vs 1000 MPa) and No Break notched Izod vs 500 J/m for B5500 3. Haldia B5500 offers higher tensile strength @ yield (27 MPa vs 25 MPa) and @ break (40 MPa)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia B5500 declares ESCR >1000 hrs (F50, 10% Igepal) — the single most important property for chemical, detergent and lube-oil containers — whereas the 52GB002 TDS states no ESCR value at all, so chemical-duty performance cannot be verified 2. B5500 is explicitly qualified up to ~120 L bulk containers and blow moulded water tanks to 1000 L, giving a documented size envelope 3. Trade-off: 52GB002 is the better parison for containers above 100 L on accumulator heads, with lower MFI (0.26 vs 0.35 g/10 min @ 5 kg) for higher melt strength and less sag on very large parts

desc: Relene 52GB003 is a High Molecular Weight High Density Polyethylene blow moulding grade with
high stiffness and impact strength and good ESCR. It possesses medium molecular weight
distribution, very good swell and easy processability. 52GB003 can readily be processed on most
HDPE blow moulding machines.
uses: Medium volume blow moulded containers, liners, sheets

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/5 kg) 0.45 g/10 min 2. MFI (190°C/21.6 kg) 8.5 g/10 min 3. Density 0.952 g/cm³ 4. Tensile Stress @ Yield 29 MPa 5. Elongation @ Yield 11% 6. Notched Izod Impact No Break 7. Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa 8. Vicat Softening Point 125 °C
competition.superior: Medium MWD HMHDPE combining high stiffness, No Break impact and good ESCR with easy processing on standard (non-accumulator) blow moulding machines.
competition.limitations: 1. ESCR is described qualitatively as good but no numerical value is given — ESCR Not available in official TDS 2. Vicat 125 °C limits continuous high-temperature service 3. Not intended for very large (>100 L) accumulator-head parts
competition.comparison: 1. Both serve medium-volume blow moulded containers 2. Reliance 52GB003 offers higher tensile strength @ yield (29 MPa vs 27 MPa) and No Break notched Izod vs 500 J/m for B5500 3. Haldia B5500 has lower MFI (0.35 vs 0.45 g/10 min @ 5 kg), giving higher melt strength for larger parisons
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia B5500 declares ESCR >1000 hrs, giving a verifiable basis for packing detergents, surfactants and lube oils; 52GB003 claims good ESCR without a number, so aggressive-chemical duty cannot be specified from the TDS 2. B5500's higher Vicat (127 °C vs 125 °C) and 20–25 °C mould-water recommendation support faster cycles on thick-wall medium containers 3. Trade-off: for stiffness-limited designs 52GB003 is stronger at yield (29 MPa vs 27 MPa), so wall thickness can be trimmed where chemical exposure is mild

desc: relatively higher density and stiffness, good flow and impact strength, good ECSR and bimodal
molecular weight distribution for easy processability. 54GB012 can readily be processed on most
HDPE blow moulding lines.
uses: Edible oil, cosmetic, personal care products and general purpose blow moulding containers, Jerry cans, DWC Pipes

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/5 kg) 1.2 g/10 min 2. Density 0.954 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 27 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 11% 5. Notched Izod Impact No Break 6. Flexural Modulus 900 MPa 7. Vicat Softening Point 127 °C
competition.superior: Bimodal MWD giving easy flow at relatively high density — allows small, detailed containers to be blown on standard lines with good ESCR.
competition.limitations: 1. ESCR described as good but no value stated — ESCR Not available in official TDS 2. Flexural Modulus 900 MPa is moderate for a 0.954 g/cm³ resin, limiting top-load in tall jerry cans 3. Not suited to large-volume accumulator-head containers
competition.comparison: 1. Both target small-to-medium rigid packaging; B6401 is specifically qualified for containers up to 20 L for lubricants and edible oils 2. Haldia B6401 is markedly stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1300 MPa vs 900 MPa) at higher density (0.960 vs 0.954 g/cm³) and stronger at yield (32 MPa vs 27 MPa) 3. Reliance 54GB012 has higher flow (MFI5 1.2 vs 1.6 g/10 min for B6401 — B6401 is actually the higher-flow grade) and No Break Izod vs 300 J/m
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia B6401's 1300 MPa flexural modulus vs 900 MPa is decisive for stacked edible-oil jerry cans, where top-load capacity rather than impact governs wall thickness — a 30%+ stiffness gain allows real down-gauging 2. Its higher Vicat (129 °C vs 127 °C) supports hot-fill and warm-warehouse stacking 3. Trade-off: B6401's ESCR is only <20 hrs, so it must NOT be substituted for cosmetic, personal-care or surfactant-contact packaging. For those contents 54GB012 or Haldia E5201 (ESCR >600 hrs) is the correct choice

desc: Relene 54GC016 is a bimodal High-Density Polyethylene grade suitable for injection and extrusion-
compression molded Caps & Closures. This grade offers excellent process ability & organoleptic
properties, very good balance of stiffness & toughness along with ESCR.
uses: Caps & Closures for Still Beverages, Food & Industrial Packaging, Shoulder for Collapsible Tubes/ Lamitubes

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 1.6 g/10 min 2. Density 0.954 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 27 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 9% 5. Elongation @ Break >900% 6. Flexural Modulus 1200 MPa 7. Hardness Shore D 62 8. Vicat Softening Point 126 °C
competition.superior: Bimodal HDPE giving excellent organoleptics with a very good stiffness–toughness balance plus ESCR, for closures without slip additive.
competition.limitations: 1. Contains no slip additive — torque release must be managed by mould design or external lubricant 2. ESCR quoted qualitatively only — ESCR Not available in official TDS 3. Notched Izod Impact Not available in official TDS
competition.comparison: 1. Both are caps-and-closure grades supplied without slip agent, for injection and compression moulding 2. Haldia M5601 offers higher tensile strength @ yield (28 MPa vs 27 MPa) and declares ESCR 400 hrs plus Notched Izod 50 J/m — values absent from the Reliance TDS 3. Reliance 54GC016 is markedly stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1200 MPa vs 1000 MPa) and has higher elongation @ break (>900% vs Not stated)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia M5601 publishes ESCR 400 hrs and Izod 50 J/m, letting a closure designer verify stress-crack life under sealing-liner compression — data the 54GC016 TDS does not provide 2. Its broad MWD from the Mitsui CX process is stated to confer good organoleptics and high ESCR specifically for CSD, water, juice and beverage closures, a wider qualified beverage envelope 3. Trade-off: Reliance 54GC016 is the stiffer resin (1200 MPa vs 1000 MPa), which better resists closure ovality and back-off torque loss on wide-mouth food jars

desc: Relene 54GC017 is a bimodal High-Density Polyethylene grade containing slip additive suitable for
injection and extrusion-compression molded Caps & Closures. This grade offers excellent
processability & organoleptic properties, very good balance of stiffness & toughness along with
ESCR for Carbonated Soft Drink Closure Applications.
uses: Caps & Closures for Beverage/Carbonated Soft Drinks, Food & Industrial Packaging, Shoulder for Collapsible Tubes/ Lamitubes

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 1.25 g/10 min 2. Density 0.951 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 27 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 9% 5. Elongation @ Break >900% 6. Flexural Modulus 1050 MPa 7. Hardness Shore D 62 8. Vicat Softening Point 126 °C
competition.superior: Bimodal HDPE containing slip additive, with the stiffness–toughness balance and ESCR required for carbonated soft drink closures.
competition.limitations: 1. ESCR reported only as >4 (units and test basis not fully stated in the TDS) — a definitive ESCR value is Not available in official TDS 2. Notched Izod Impact Not available in official TDS 3. Slip additive present, so the grade is unsuitable where printing or secondary decoration demands an additive-free surface
competition.comparison: 1. Both are slip-additivated closure grades aimed at carbonated soft drink applications 2. Haldia M5601S declares ESCR 400 hrs and Notched Izod 50 J/m, against an unclear >4 ESCR figure and no Izod value in the Reliance TDS 3. Haldia M5601S is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa vs 1050 MPa for Reliance — comparable) and stronger at yield (28 MPa vs 27 MPa) at higher density (0.954 vs 0.951 g/cm³)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia M5601S states a quantified ESCR of 400 hrs, which is the property that governs closure cracking under CO₂ pressure and liner compression; the 54GC017 ESCR entry (>4) cannot be used for design verification 2. Its slip agent is specified as being for better torque release, matching the CSD removal-torque window 3. Trade-off: the two are otherwise close on stiffness and hardness, and 54GC017 has the higher declared elongation @ break (>900%), which favours resistance to closure skirt tearing on aggressive capping heads

desc: Relene 2002F is a high molecular weight, high-density polyethylene (HDPE) grade, typically
designed for blow molded automotive fuel tank & gas cylinder applications. This grade can also
be used for medium blow molding application. The grade demonstrates very high Environmental
Stress Cracking Resistance (ESCR), good chemical resistance in combination with an excellent
low temperature properties. Its high melt strength helps in production of multi-layer tanks by blow
molding. This grade exhibits outstanding resistance particularly to ethanol blended gasoline.
uses: This grade is specially designed for blow molded Automotive fuel tanks, Gas cylinders, Medium blow molding containers etc

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/21.6 kg) 5.5 g/10 min 2. Density 0.947 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 24 MPa 4. Tensile Strength @ Break 39 MPa 5. Elongation @ Yield 9% 6. Elongation @ Break 800% 7. Flexural Modulus 880 MPa 8. ESCR (F50) >1000 hrs
competition.superior: Very high ESCR (>1000 hrs) with good chemical resistance and excellent low-temperature properties — the combination required for automotive fuel tanks and gas cylinders.
competition.limitations: 1. Highly specialised — over-specified and uneconomic for general purpose containers 2. Notched Izod Impact and Vicat Softening Point Not available in official TDS 3. Low flexural modulus (880 MPa) means tank geometry, not resin stiffness, must carry structural load
competition.comparison: 1. Haldia has no fuel-tank or gas-cylinder qualified HMWHDPE in the supplied portfolio; B5500 is the closest large-part blow moulding grade 2. Both declare ESCR >1000 hrs; Haldia B5500 is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa vs 880 MPa) and stronger at yield (27 MPa vs 24 MPa) 3. Reliance 2002F has the lower density (0.947 vs 0.952 g/cm³) and higher elongation @ break (800%) that support the low-temperature ductility a fuel tank requires
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia is NOT better for this application. B5500 is qualified for chemicals, detergents, lube oils and water tanks — it carries no hydrocarbon-permeation, low-temperature-impact or fuel-tank qualification, and the supplied TDS makes no automotive fuel system claim 2. The honest trade-off: B5500 can substitute only for the medium blow moulding containers listed as a secondary use of 2002F, where its higher stiffness (1000 vs 880 MPa) and 500 J/m Izod are genuine advantages 3. For automotive fuel tanks and gas cylinders there is no technically suitable Haldia alternative in the supplied range
competition.alt_note: B5500 (closest available — not an equivalent)

desc: Relene B56003 is a High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) grade suitable for general purpose extrusion
blow moulding applications. Articles made from this grade exhibit good stiffness. The resin offers
good melt strength, ESCR and impact resistance and typically used for general purpose containers
and jerry cans for packaging of oil, vanaspati, etc.
uses: General purpose containers, jerry cans up to 20 L for packaging of oil, vanaspati, etc

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/5 kg) 1.5 g/10 min 2. Density 0.956 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 26 MPa 4. Elongation @ Break 550% 5. Flexural Modulus 900 MPa 6. Hardness Shore D 69 7. Vicat Softening Point 128 °C
competition.superior: Good melt strength, ESCR and impact resistance at high density — a general purpose extrusion blow moulding workhorse for oil and vanaspati packaging.
competition.limitations: 1. ESCR and impact resistance described qualitatively — no numerical values; ESCR and Notched Izod Not available in official TDS 2. Elongation @ break 550% is modest, limiting drop performance of filled 20 L cans 3. Flexural Modulus 900 MPa is low for 0.956 g/cm³ density, limiting stacking load
competition.comparison: 1. Both are general purpose blow moulding grades for edible oil and lubricant containers up to 20 L 2. Haldia B6401 is substantially stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1300 MPa vs 900 MPa), stronger at yield (32 MPa vs 26 MPa) and declares Notched Izod 300 J/m, which B56003 does not state 3. Haldia B6401 has higher density (0.960 vs 0.956 g/cm³) and Vicat (129 °C vs 128 °C)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia B6401's 1300 MPa flexural modulus against 900 MPa is a direct top-load advantage for palletised 20 L oil jerry cans — the load case that actually fails in the warehouse — and permits genuine wall down-gauging 2. Its declared 300 J/m notched Izod gives a verifiable drop-impact basis for filled cans, absent from the B56003 TDS 3. Trade-off: B6401's ESCR is <20 hrs. For vanaspati and refined edible oils this is acceptable, but B6401 must not be carried across to detergent or surfactant contents, where Haldia E5201 (ESCR >600 hrs) is required instead

desc: Relene E52009 is a High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) grade with low gel content, excellent
orientation characteristic and negligible water carry-over. This grade is recommended for making
raffia tapes and monofilaments (Diameter >0.20 mm) with excellent balance of high tenacity and
good elongation.
uses: Oriented tapes, woven sacks and monofilaments

props.name: Tear Strength (MD / TD) ASTM D1922 g/µm

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/5 kg) 0.90 g/10 min 2. Density 0.952 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 35 / 38 MPa (MD/TD) 4. Elongation @ Break 900 / 950% (MD/TD) 5. Tear Strength 0.6 / 1.7 (MD/TD)
competition.superior: Low gel content, excellent orientation characteristics and negligible water carry-over, giving a high-tenacity / high-elongation balance on tape and monofilament lines.
competition.limitations: 1. Flexural Modulus, Notched Izod and Vicat Softening Point Not available in official TDS 2. Restricted to monofilament diameters above 0.20 mm 3. Application-specific — not a general purpose moulding or film grade
competition.haldia_alt: HD T9 (tape / raffia) and HD T10S (monofilament)
competition.comparison: 1. Reliance E52009 covers tape and monofilament in one grade; Haldia splits the duty — HD T9 for stretched tape / raffia, HD T10S for monofilament for nets, twines and ropes 2. Haldia grades run at higher flow (MFI 1.1 g/10 min @ 2.16 kg; 3 g/10 min @ 5 kg) against 0.90 g/10 min @ 5 kg for Reliance 3. Haldia declares Notched Izod 400 J/m, Flexural Modulus 1100 MPa (HD T9) / 1000 MPa (HD T10S) and Elongation @ Break 1100% — a fuller dataset than E52009 provides
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia HD T9 and HD T10S publish complete stretch-line parameters — barrel 200–240 °C, die 230–250 °C, quench 30 °C and, for HD T10S, a ~98 °C water stretching temperature — which is exactly the data a raffia or monofilament processor needs to set up a line; the Reliance TDS gives only a single 180–220 °C band 2. Their declared 1100% elongation @ break gives more stretch-ratio headroom before tape fibrillation than the 900/950% of E52009 3. Trade-off: two Haldia grades are needed to replace one Reliance grade, so a converter running both tape and monofilament on shared silos loses the single-resin simplicity that E52009 offers

desc: Relene F46003 is a High Density Polyethylene grade suitable for general purpose blown film &
extrusion blow moulding applications. Articles blown from this grade exhibit moderate to good
stiffness. The resin offers good melt strength, ESCR and impact resistance.
uses: Used for producing blown film in carry bags and co-extruded film structures, general purpose blow molded containers

props.name: Tear Strength (MD / TD) ASTM D1922 g/µm

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 0.38 g/10 min 2. Density 0.946 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 29 / 26 MPa (MD/TD) 4. Elongation @ Break 780 / 950% (MD/TD) 5. Dart Impact Strength 1.8 6. Tear Strength 0.4 / 4.5 (MD/TD)
competition.superior: Dual-capability resin offering good melt strength, ESCR and impact resistance for both blown film and extrusion blow moulding on the same silo.
competition.limitations: 1. ESCR quoted qualitatively — ESCR Not available in official TDS 2. Flexural Modulus and Vicat Softening Point Not available in official TDS 3. Moderate stiffness at 0.946 g/cm³ — not a high-barrier or high-stiffness film grade
competition.comparison: 1. Both are dual film / blow moulding HDPE grades; E5201 is recommended for high-ESCR blow moulding, lamination film, general purpose film and extrusion 2. Haldia E5201 declares ESCR >600 hrs, Notched Izod 120 J/m, Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa and Vicat 122 °C — all absent from the F46003 TDS 3. Reliance F46003 has the lower density (0.946 vs 0.950 g/cm³), favouring film toughness and drawdown
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia E5201 quantifies ESCR at >600 hrs, which is what qualifies a resin for cable sheathing and chemical-contact blow moulded containers; F46003's unquantified ESCR claim cannot support those uses 2. E5201 adds cable sheathing and jacketing compound to the same grade's application list, widening reuse across film, blow moulding and wire-and-cable lines from a single silo 3. Trade-off: E5201's much higher flow (MFI 0.35 g/10 min @ 2.16 kg vs 0.38 — comparable, but MFI21.6 of 32 vs Not stated) and lower melt strength make F46003 the safer parison for deeper-draw blow moulded parts

desc: Relene F60003 is a High Density Polyethylene grade suitable for use in blends in coextruded oriented
film application. This grade is designed to improve stiffness and barrier requirement in films. This
resin offers good balance of mechanical and optical properties.
uses: Blown film for use in food packaging, e- commerce and other packaging applications

props.name: Tear Strength (MD / TD) ASTM D1922 g/µm

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 0.7 g/10 min 2. Density 0.957 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 29 / 26 MPa (MD/TD) 4. Elongation @ Break 780 / 950% (MD/TD) 5. Dart Impact Strength 1.8 6. Tear Strength 0.4 / 4.5 (MD/TD)
competition.superior: High density (0.957 g/cm³) designed for use in blends and co-extruded oriented (MDO) film structures to raise stiffness and barrier.
competition.limitations: 1. Designed for use in blends — not optimised as a stand-alone film resin 2. Flexural Modulus, Notched Izod, Vicat and Haze Not available in official TDS 3. High density limits film toughness where high dart impact is the governing requirement
competition.comparison: 1. Both are high-density HDPE film grades; HD T6 is a general purpose extrusion and lamination film grade at 0.960 g/cm³ vs 0.957 g/cm³ for Reliance 2. Haldia HD T6 has lower flow (MFI 0.50 vs 0.70 g/10 min @ 2.16 kg), giving higher melt strength on the bubble 3. Haldia HD T6 declares Flexural Modulus 1150 MPa, Notched Izod 250 J/m, Tensile Strength @ Break 38 MPa and Vicat 124 °C — none of which F60003 states
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia HD T6's declared 1150 MPa flexural modulus and 0.960 g/cm³ density deliver the film stiffness and moisture barrier that F60003 is blended in to provide, but as verifiable numbers rather than a qualitative claim 2. Its lower MFI (0.50 vs 0.70 g/10 min) gives better bubble stability at high blow-up ratio, which matters on thin-gauge e-commerce film 3. Trade-off: HD T6 is not qualified for MDO orientation lines, and F60003 is explicitly designed for co-extruded oriented structures — so for true MDO film the Reliance grade remains the correct choice

desc: Relene F60080 is a High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) grade suitable for film extrusion applications
where higher stiffness, along with good processability is required. This grade can be used in blends
with LLDPE and LDPE and can be co-extruded. Grade is designed to cater hygiene film applications
where gel free films are required.
uses: Cast Film applications like Hygiene films

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 8.0 g/10 min 2. Density 0.960 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Break 30 / 28 MPa (MD/TD) 4. Elongation @ Break 850 / 800% (MD/TD) 5. Vicat Softening Point 127 °C 6. Haze 12%
competition.superior: Gel-free high-flow HDPE formulated for hygiene cast film, blendable with LLDPE and LDPE and co-extrudable.
competition.limitations: 1. Haze 12% — not suitable where high clarity is required 2. Flexural Modulus and Notched Izod Not available in official TDS 3. High MFI (8.0 g/10 min) gives low melt strength — not usable on blown film lines
competition.haldia_alt: No technically suitable Haldia grade in the supplied range (HD T6 is the nearest HDPE film grade)
competition.comparison: 1. Haldia's supplied portfolio contains no HDPE cast film grade; HD T6 is a blown extrusion and lamination film grade 2. The processing gap is decisive: F60080 runs at MFI 8.0 g/10 min for chill-roll casting, whereas HD T6 is MFI 0.50 g/10 min — a sixteen-fold difference in flow that cannot be bridged by temperature adjustment 3. Both sit at high density (0.960 g/cm³) and similar Vicat (127 °C vs 124 °C), so the resins are comparable in stiffness class but not in process suitability
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia is NOT better here — it has no equivalent. HD T6 cannot be substituted on a cast film line: at MFI 0.50 g/10 min it would not draw down to hygiene-film gauge and would overload the extruder 2. The only genuine overlap is as a high-density stiffness component in blends, where HD T6 could serve if the line is blown rather than cast 3. For gel-free hygiene cast film there is no technically suitable Haldia alternative in the supplied range
competition.alt_note: No technically suitable Haldia grade in the supplied range (HD T6 is the nearest HDPE film grade)

desc: Relene HD50MA180 is a high flow High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) grade. This grade is specially
formulated to manufacture large, intricate, thin walled multi cavity injection moulded products. It has
narrow molecular weight distribution, which makes it easier to process and products manufactured
have good gloss and rigidity.
uses: Houseware, storage bins, thin walled article

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 20.0 g/10 min 2. Density 0.950 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 22 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 12% 5. Flexural Modulus 900 MPa 6. Vicat Softening Point 123 °C
competition.superior: High flow with narrow MWD for easy filling of large, intricate, thin-walled multi-cavity mouldings with good gloss and rigidity.
competition.limitations: 1. Notched Izod Impact and ESCR Not available in official TDS 2. High MFI (20 g/10 min) gives inherently low impact strength — unsuitable for heavy-duty crates or drop-critical parts 3. Tensile strength @ yield 22 MPa is modest for load-bearing mouldings
competition.comparison: 1. Direct match on flow and density — both MFI 20 g/10 min @ 2.16 kg at 0.950 g/cm³, and both are positioned as general purpose injection moulding grades 2. Reliance HD50MA180 is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 900 MPa vs 800 MPa), stronger at yield (22 MPa vs 22 MPa — equal) and has higher Vicat (123 °C vs 121 °C) 3. Haldia M5018L declares Notched Izod 35 J/m, Elongation @ Break 450% and HDT 64 °C — values the Reliance TDS omits
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia M5018L publishes the Notched Izod figure (35 J/m) and HDT (64 °C) that a moulder needs to predict bin and houseware drop performance and hot-warehouse deflection; HD50MA180 states neither 2. Its declared nozzle temperature of 235 °C and barrel range 180–235 °C give a tighter, more actionable setup window than the single 180–220 °C band quoted by Reliance 3. Trade-off: Haldia is not better on stiffness — HD50MA180's 900 MPa flexural modulus against 800 MPa is a real advantage for thin-wall storage bins, where panel rigidity rather than impact governs the design

desc: Relene HD53EA010 is a High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) grade produced and specially formulated
to manufacture stretched tape products and other extrusion products with good combination of
tenacity and elongation. It has very good processability and stretch-ability, less motor load and high
output combined with good tape properties to make it a grade of choice.

props.name: Tear Strength (MD / TD) ASTM D1922 g/µm

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 1.0 g/10 min 2. Density 0.955 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 33 / 36 MPa (MD/TD) 4. Elongation @ Break 900 / 950% (MD/TD) 5. Tear Strength 0.6 / 1.7 (MD/TD)
competition.superior: Very good stretchability with low motor load and high output, giving a strong tenacity–elongation combination on stretched tape lines.
competition.limitations: 1. Flexural Modulus, Notched Izod and Vicat Softening Point Not available in official TDS 2. Dedicated tape grade — not suitable for moulding or film 3. Stretch ratio and oven/quench settings not specified in the TDS
competition.comparison: 1. Close application match — both are HDPE stretched tape / raffia grades for woven fabric 2. Comparable flow: MFI 1.0 g/10 min for Reliance vs 1.1 g/10 min for HD T9 @ 2.16 kg; Reliance runs at higher density (0.955 vs 0.950 g/cm³) 3. Haldia HD T9 declares Notched Izod 400 J/m, Flexural Modulus 1100 MPa, Elongation @ Break 1100% and Vicat 127 °C — a fuller dataset than HD53EA010 provides
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia HD T9 specifies the complete raffia line setup — barrel 200–240 °C, die 230–250 °C, quench 30 °C — whereas the Reliance TDS quotes only a generic 180–220 °C processing band that is below the die temperature a raffia line actually runs 2. Its 1100% elongation @ break against 900/950% gives greater stretch-ratio latitude before tape fibrillation, which raises achievable tape tenacity on the same line 3. Trade-off: HD53EA010 has the higher declared tape tensile (33/36 MPa MD/TD vs 26 MPa yield for HD T9, though measured on different specimen bases) and higher density, so it is competitive where sack fabric strength per gram is the target

desc: Relene HD55EF010 is a High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) grade, specially formulated to manufacture
oriented monofilament products. It has narrow molecular weight distribution and has very good
processability, less motor load and high output combined with very good elongation and filament
properties to make it a grade of choice.
uses: Monofilaments for mosquito nets, fishing nets etc

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 1.0 g/10 min 2. Density 0.955 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 23 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 15% 5. Notched Izod Impact No Break 6. Flexural Modulus 820 MPa 7. Vicat Softening Point 127 °C
competition.superior: Narrow MWD giving very good processability with low motor load, high output and the high elongation needed for fine oriented monofilament.
competition.limitations: 1. ESCR Not available in official TDS 2. Low flexural modulus (820 MPa) — a soft, extensible grade not suited to rigid applications 3. Dedicated monofilament grade; not intended for tape, film or moulding
competition.comparison: 1. Direct application match — HD T10S is a HDPE monofilament grade for nets, twines and ropes 2. Haldia HD T10S has higher flow (MFI 1.1 vs 1.0 g/10 min @ 2.16 kg) at lower density (0.950 vs 0.955 g/cm³) 3. Haldia HD T10S is markedly stiffer and stronger (Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa vs 820 MPa; Tensile Strength @ Yield 26 MPa vs 23 MPa; @ Break 38 MPa) with Elongation @ Break 1100% and Izod 400 J/m
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia HD T10S delivers higher filament tenacity — 26 MPa at yield and 38 MPa at break against 23 MPa at yield for HD55EF010 — which directly raises net and twine breaking load at equal denier 2. It specifies the ~98 °C hot-water stretching temperature and 200–240 °C barrel / 230–250 °C die profile that a monofilament line is actually set to; the Reliance TDS gives only 180–220 °C 3. Trade-off: HD55EF010's lower modulus (820 MPa vs 1000 MPa) and No Break Izod make it the softer, more drapeable filament, which is preferable for mosquito netting where hand feel matters more than breaking load

desc: Relene L60075 is a High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) grade suitable for injection moulding
applications where good mechanical properties are essential with gloss, dimensional stability, good
ESCR, required for technical moulding like moulded crates, luggage shells, helmets, defense
applications, etc. L60075 is suitable for applications where articles are exposed to sunlight e.g. soft
drink crates, defense applications, helmets, industrial pails, etc.
uses: Crates, Industrial Pails and defense applications

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 8.0 g/10 min 2. Density 0.960 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 25 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 15% 5. Flexural Modulus 900 MPa 6. Hardness Shore D 69 7. Vicat Softening Point 128 °C
competition.superior: High density with good gloss, dimensional stability and ESCR, and stated suitability for articles exposed to sunlight such as soft drink crates.
competition.limitations: 1. ESCR described qualitatively — ESCR Not available in official TDS 2. Notched Izod Impact Not available in official TDS 3. UV protection level not quantified in the TDS; outdoor service life cannot be verified from published data
competition.comparison: 1. Both target heavy-duty injection moulded crates and industrial products intended for outdoor exposure 2. Comparable flow — MFI 8.0 g/10 min for Reliance vs 7.5 g/10 min for M6007LU @ 2.16 kg; Reliance runs at higher density (0.960 vs 0.950 g/cm³) 3. Reliance L60075 is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 900 MPa vs 850 MPa), harder (Shore D 69 vs 62) and stronger at yield (25 MPa vs 24 MPa); Haldia M6007LU declares Notched Izod 50 J/m and Elongation @ Break 800%
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia M6007LU states that it is stabilised with HALS+ to give long service life under outdoor exposure — a named stabiliser system, against an unquantified sunlight-suitability claim in the L60075 TDS; for soft-drink crates in open yards this is the difference between a verifiable and an unverifiable weathering specification 2. Its declared 50 J/m Izod and 800% elongation @ break give a documented basis for crate drop and stacking-corner performance 3. Trade-off: L60075 is objectively the stiffer, harder resin (900 MPa and Shore D 69 vs 850 MPa and Shore D 62), so for pails and defence mouldings where rigidity and surface hardness govern, Reliance is the better choice

desc: Relene M60075 is a High - Density Polyethylene (HDPE) grade suitable for injection moulding
applications where good mechanical properties are essential with gloss, dimensional stability, good
ESCR, required for crates, luggage shells, helmets, defense applications, etc.

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 8.0 g/10 min 2. Density 0.960 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 25 MPa 4. Elongation @ Break 800% 5. Flexural Modulus 900 MPa 6. Hardness Shore D 69 7. Vicat Softening Point 128 °C

desc: Relene 16MA400 is a Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) with a high melt flow index for very thin,

making variety of masterbatches.
uses: Lids, Powder Coating, Injection Molding Articles, Masterbatches etc

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 30 g/10 min 2. Density 0.918 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 10 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 40% 5. Notched Izod Impact No Break 6. Flexural Modulus 140 MPa 7. Vicat Softening Point 84 °C
competition.superior: Very high melt flow (MFI 30) with No Break notched Izod — fills very thin, intricate, large mouldings and acts as a low-melting carrier for masterbatch.

Flow is closely matched — M5025L is MFI 30 g/10 min @ 2.16 kg, identical to 16MA400 3. competition.alt_note: No LDPE grade in the supplied Haldia range (M5025L is the nearest masterbatch-capable grade)

desc: Relene 22FA002 is a Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) heavy duty film grade produced using high

Environmental Stress Crack Resistance (ESCR), mechanical and impact resistance.

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 0.2 g/10 min 2. Density 0.920 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Break 26 / 24 MPa (MD/TD) 4. Elongation @ Break 400 / 600% (MD/TD) 5. Dart Impact Strength F50 5.5 g/µm

Reliance 22FA002 has the higher dart impact (5.5 g/µm vs 4.0 g/µm) and higher tensile @ break (26/24 MPa vs 25/16 MPa MD/TD); Haldia 71501S has the far higher TD tear (16 g/µ vs Not stated for Reliance)

On the two properties both TDS declare, Reliance leads: dart impact 5.5 g/µm against 4.0 g/µm and MD tensile @ break 26 MPa against 25 MPa 2. For shrink film the substitution fails on principle: LLDPE does not develop the same shrink tension as LDPE regardless of grade selection 3. 71501S is a reasonable alternative only for the general-purpose heavy bag portion of the application, where its declared TD tear of 16 g/µ genuinely helps resist tear propagation, and is best used in blend with LDPE rather than as a drop-in replacement
competition.alt_note: No LDPE grade in the supplied Haldia range (71501S is the nearest packaging film grade)

desc: Relene 24FS040 is a Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) that can be used in blown film application
due to excellent processability. This grade is formulated with slip additive for good surface slip and
openability.
uses: Shopping bag, General Purpose Packaging etc

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 4.0 g/10 min 2. Density 0.920 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Break 18 / 16 MPa (MD/TD) 4. Elongation @ Break 250 / 400% (MD/TD) 5. Haze 7% 6. Gloss >100 7. Dart Impact Strength F50 2.0 g/µm

competition.comparison: 1. Closest functional match — 71602S is a LLDPE general purpose packaging film grade additivated with slip and antiblock for good openability and slip, the same functional role as 24FS040 2. Flow is reasonably matched: 71602S is MFI 2.0 g/10 min vs 4.0 g/10 min for Reliance @ 2.16 kg 3. Haldia 71602S offers higher dart impact (3 g/µm vs 2.0 g/µm), higher tensile @ break (19/14 MPa vs 18/16 MPa MD/TD) and declares Tear 4/12 g/µ (MD/TD), which 24FS040 does not state; the Reliance grade declares the better optics (Haze 7%, Gloss >100)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia 71602S delivers 50% higher dart impact (3 g/µm vs 2.0 g/µm) at half the melt flow index, meaning a shopping bag of the same gauge carries more drop energy before puncture — the failure mode that actually matters for carrier bags 2. Its declared TD tear of 12 g/µ gives a verifiable resistance to tear propagation from a nicked edge, a figure absent from the 24FS040 TDS, and its published bubble setup (blow-up ratio 2.0–3.0, die gap 2.0–2.5 mm, melt 190–200 °C) transfers directly to the line 3. Trade-off: 71602S is LLDPE, not LDPE. It will not match the Gloss >100 and Haze 7% optics of 24FS040, and its lower MFI raises motor load, so for high-gloss printed retail bags the Reliance grade remains optically superior

desc: Relene 1005FY20 is a Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) is specially designed for production of

easy open ability and smooth flow of film on packaging machines.
uses: Slip grade for Mono, Co-extruded Films for Liquid Packaging, General Purpose Consumer Product Packaging

Flow differs — 71501S is MFI 1.0 g/10 min vs 0.5 g/10 min for 1005FY20 @ 2.16 kg 3. Haldia 71501S offers higher dart impact (4.0 g/µm vs 3.7 g/µm), higher MD tensile @ break (25 MPa vs 21 MPa) and declares Tear 6/16 g/µ and Gloss 76; Reliance declares Haze 8% and Gloss >80
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia 71501S gives higher film toughness on the measures that govern milk pouch failure — dart impact 4.0 g/µm against 3.7 g/µm and MD tensile @ break 25 MPa against 21 MPa — so the pouch survives more drops at the same 50–60 micron gauge 2. Its declared TD tear of 16 g/µ provides tear-propagation data the Reliance TDS omits, and its published blow-up ratio 2.0–3.0 and die gap 2.0–2.5 mm give the FFS converter a verified bubble geometry 3. Trade-off: this is a polymer-class substitution, not an equivalent. 1005FY20 is the LDPE seal and processing modifier in the structure; 71501S is LLDPE and cannot by itself supply the LDPE melt strength and seal behaviour the FFS machine is set up for. Haldia offers no LDPE to fill that role

desc: Relene 1020FA20 is a Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) film grade and can be processed easily on
conventional blown film and cast film lines. This grade is designed to facilitate adhesion during
lamination.
uses: Hygiene Film, Bubble Wrap Film, Adhesive Lamination Film etc

competition.comparison: 1. Closest functional match — 71601W is Haldia's LLDPE blown film grade for general purpose adhesive lamination films and is explicitly supplied without slip or antiblock additives, the correct surface state for lamination 2. Flow differs: 71601W is MFI 1.0 g/10 min vs 2.0 g/10 min for 1020FA20 @ 2.16 kg 3. Haldia 71601W offers higher dart impact (4.0 g/µm vs 3.0 g/µm), higher MD tensile @ break (25 MPa vs 21 MPa), Tear 6/16 g/µ and Gloss 76 vs 60 for Reliance
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia 71601W is additive-free by specification, which removes the risk of slip migration destroying adhesive bond strength — the classic failure mode in lamination film; the Reliance TDS does not confirm the additive state of 1020FA20 2. Its higher dart impact (4.0 g/µm vs 3.0 g/µm), higher MD tensile at break (25 MPa vs 21 MPa) and higher gloss (76 vs 60) give more machine-direction tension latitude on the laminator and a brighter laminate face 3. Trade-off: 71601W is LLDPE and is specified for blown film only. For the cast film and bubble wrap portion of 1020FA20's duty, and for LDPE-level melt strength and optics (Haze 7%), the Reliance grade remains the better fit

desc: Relene 1070LA17 is a Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) used in extrusion coating produced using
high pressure autoclave process. This grade is specially developed for extrusion coating on
different substrates and contains no additives. It exhibits excellent drawdown characteristics
maintaining good adhesion, with very low neck-in even at higher line speeds. It can also be easily
processed into thin gauge films for adhesive lamination, heat & pressure lamination.
uses: Extrusion Coating, Heat & Pressure Lamination Film etc

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 8.5 g/10 min 2. Density 0.917 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Break 18 / 15 MPa (MD/TD) 4. Elongation @ Break 250 / 400% (MD/TD)

competition.comparison: 1. Close application match — 72307E is Haldia's LLDPE for extrusion coating on HDPE woven fabric, aluminium foil, jute, paper and allied substrates 2. Flow is well matched: 72307E is MFI 7.0 g/10 min vs 8.5 g/10 min for 1070LA17 @ 2.16 kg, at 0.926 vs 0.917 g/cm³ 3. Haldia 72307E declares Notched Izod 500 J/m, Flexural Modulus 300 MPa, Tensile Strength @ Break 18 MPa and Vicat 102 °C — mechanical data the Reliance coating TDS omits
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia 72307E specifies the coating line directly — barrel 200–270 °C and die 250–280 °C — a narrower and lower window than the 200–320 °C quoted for 1070LA17, which reduces resin oxidation and smoke at the die lip on long runs 2. Its 500 J/m notched Izod gives coated woven sacks measurably better resistance to coating crack-off at fold lines 3. Trade-off: Haldia is NOT better on neck-in. An autoclave LDPE such as 1070LA17 has long-chain branching that LLDPE cannot match, so 72307E will show more neck-in and poorer drawdown at high line speed, and is normally run in blend with LDPE rather than alone

Flow is closer here: 71501S at MFI 1.0 g/10 min vs 0.65 g/10 min for J1005FY20 @ 2.16 kg 3. Haldia 71501S offers higher dart impact (4.0 g/µm vs 3.2 g/µm), higher MD tensile @ break (25 MPa vs 23 MPa), Tear 6/16 g/µ and Gloss 76
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia 71501S improves the toughness metrics that govern milk pouch failure — dart 4.0 g/µm against 3.2 g/µm and MD tensile at break 25 MPa against 23 MPa — while sitting closer in flow to J1005FY20 than to the lower-MFI J1005FS20, making it the better of the two substitutions 2. Slip and antiblock are specified for openability, matching the FFS machine's film-separation requirement, and its declared TD tear of 16 g/µ quantifies seal-edge tear resistance 3. competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 0.7 g/10 min 2. Density 0.923 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Break 21 / 20 MPa (MD/TD) 4. Elongation @ Break 250 / 500% (MD/TD) 5. Haze 7% 6. Gloss 60 7. Dart Impact Strength F50 3.1 g/µm

competition.comparison: 1. 71601W matches the lamination film half of the duty — LLDPE blown film for general purpose adhesive lamination, supplied without slip or antiblock 2. Flow differs: 71601W at MFI 1.0 g/10 min vs 0.7 g/10 min for J1007FA20 @ 2.16 kg 3. Haldia 71601W offers higher dart impact (4.0 g/µm vs 3.1 g/µm), higher MD tensile @ break (25 MPa vs 21 MPa), Tear 6/16 g/µ and Gloss 76 vs 60 for Reliance
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. For the lamination film portion Haldia 71601W is better: it is specified additive-free so adhesive bond strength is protected, and it carries higher dart impact (4.0 g/µm vs 3.1 g/µm), higher MD tensile at break (25 MPa vs 21 MPa) and higher gloss (76 vs 60) for laminator web tension and laminate appearance 2. For the foam portion Haldia is NOT better — there is no foam grade in the supplied range, and LLDPE lacks the long-chain branching that gives LDPE the extensional melt strength needed for uniform cell growth 3. This grade therefore splits: substitute 71601W for lamination film only, and retain an LDPE for foam blending

desc: Relene J1020FA20 is a Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) film grade and can be processed easily on

competition.comparison: 1. Direct functional match — 71601W is Haldia's LLDPE grade for general purpose adhesive lamination films, supplied without slip or antiblock 2. Flow differs: 71601W at MFI 1.0 g/10 min vs 2.0 g/10 min for J1020FA20 @ 2.16 kg 3. Haldia 71601W offers double the dart impact (4.0 g/µm vs 2.0 g/µm), higher MD tensile @ break (25 MPa vs 21 MPa), Tear 6/16 g/µ and Gloss 76 vs 60 for Reliance
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia 71601W's specified additive-free surface directly protects lamination bond strength, which slip migration otherwise degrades over roll storage — the most common lamination defect 2. It doubles dart impact (4.0 g/µm vs 2.0 g/µm) and raises MD tensile at break to 25 MPa from 21 MPa, giving substantially greater web tension latitude on the laminator and allowing faster line speeds without necking; its declared TD tear of 16 g/µ further resists edge-nick propagation 3. Trade-off: 71601W is specified for blown film only and, as LLDPE, will not match LDPE melt strength on cast lines or the bubble wrap forming step, so the cast and bubble-wrap portions of this grade's duty are not covered

desc: Relene J1020FF20 is a Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) used in foam as well as film applications.
This grade has very good melt strength which provide uniform cell structure, cell growth and
stiffness in the foam. This grade can be used in making foam using both physical and chemical

The nearest film grade, 71601W, matches only the secondary adhesive-lamination film use at MFI 1.0 vs 1.8 g/10 min

Substituting any linear polyethylene would give cell collapse and coarse, non-uniform cell structure regardless of blowing agent or die design 2. The only defensible partial substitution is 71601W for the adhesive lamination film listed as a secondary application 3. For mattress, automotive and footwear foam there is no technically suitable Haldia alternative in the supplied range

desc: Relene J1020XA20 is a Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE) used as base resin for manufacturing of
medium voltage cable insulation with suitable doses of cross linking agents. This grade is designed

competition.haldia_alt: No technically suitable Haldia grade in the supplied range
competition.comparison: 1. Haldia's supplied portfolio contains no wire and cable insulation base resin and no LDPE 2. The nearest cable-related Haldia grade is E5201, which is a HDPE recommended for cable sheathing and jacketing compound — a mechanically protective outer layer, not an electrical insulation layer 3. E5201 at 0.950 g/cm³ and Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa is far stiffer than the 0.918 g/cm³, Shore D 45 insulation resin required
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia is NOT better — it has no equivalent. Sheathing and insulation are different functions: sheathing resists abrasion and moisture, insulation must meet dielectric and cleanliness requirements that E5201's TDS does not address 2. Substituting a HDPE sheathing grade into an MV insulation layer would be an electrical-safety failure, not merely a performance compromise 3. For medium voltage cable insulation there is no technically suitable Haldia alternative in the supplied range

Its 500 J/m notched Izod and 300 MPa flexural modulus give coated woven sacks better resistance to coating crack-off at fold lines and fabric edges 3. Trade-off: the two are near-equivalents. Haldia is NOT better on optics or process fit. F17030's 0.7% haze is a cast-film-specific property that 71602W, tuned for blown film with a 2.0–3.0 blow-up ratio, will not reproduce; a blown grade run on a chill-roll caster gives poorer gauge uniformity 3. Its published bubble setup (blow-up ratio 2.0–3.0, die gap 2.0–2.5 mm, melt 190–210 °C) transfers directly to the line, where the Reliance TDS gives only 180–220 °C 4. Haldia 71501S declares Tensile Strength @ Break 25/16 MPa and Gloss 76; Reliance declares yield 12.5/12 MPa and Haze 14%

Haldia 71501S delivers higher dart impact (4.0 g/µm vs 3.5 g/µm) and higher tear in both directions (MD 6 vs 3.3 g/µ, TD 16 vs 10.3 g/µ) at the same MFI and density, so liner bags resist both puncture and tear propagation better at equal gauge 2. competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia 71601D declares ESCR 1000 hrs, which is the governing property for drip laterals exposed to fertiliser and chemigation solutions in the field — data the JD22010 TDS omits entirely 2. Its Tensile Strength @ Break of 30 MPa against 20 MPa gives a 50% higher burst margin at the same wall thickness, and 400 MPa flexural modulus supports emitter seating without lateral collapse 3. Its dedicated extrusion profile — barrel 200–240 °C, die 240–250 °C — is well above the generic 180–220 °C Reliance band and reflects the higher melt temperature drip lateral lines actually run 4. Trade-off: JD22010 declares 1000% elongation @ break and explicit IS 12786:2024 compliance; the Haldia TDS does not cite that Indian standard, so BIS-certified projects would need that compliance confirmed separately

M5018L matches only on flow — MFI 20 g/10 min, identical to M24200 — which the grade-matching brief rejects as a sufficient basis 3. designed for rotational molding application. This grade can be used for producing special products
like automotive component, manholes, diesel fuel tanks, insulated fish crates, and pallets. Due to
presence of octene co-monomer and medium density of the polymer, it exhibits excellent
toughness, impact resistance and Environmental Stress Crack Resistance (ESCR).
uses: Diesel fuel tanks, chemical storage tanks, septic tanks, general purpose tanks

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 4.5 g/10 min 2. Density 0.933 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 15 MPa 4. Elongation @ Break 950% 5. Notched Izod Impact No Break 6. Flexural Modulus 500 MPa 7. Hardness Shore D 57 8. Vicat Softening Point 115 °C
competition.superior: Octene co-monomer at medium density giving excellent toughness and impact resistance for demanding roto moulded parts including diesel fuel tanks.
competition.limitations: 1. ESCR quoted qualitatively — ESCR Not available in official TDS 2. No UV stabiliser stated — outdoor tanks require added UV package 3. Octene grade — premium cost relative to butene roto grades
competition.comparison: 1. 73204T is Haldia's LLDPE roto moulding grade for tanks and containers, at MFI 5.0 g/10 min and 0.932 g/cm³ vs 4.5 g/10 min and 0.933 g/cm³ for O35042 — density is very closely matched 2. Haldia 73204T declares Notched Izod 500 J/m and ESCR 500 hrs; Reliance declares No Break notched Izod and no ESCR figure 3. Reliance O35042 is markedly stiffer (Flexural Modulus 500 MPa vs 400 MPa), harder (Shore D 57) and higher in Vicat (115 °C vs 109 °C)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia 73204T declares ESCR of 500 hrs — the critical property for chemical and septic tank duty — which the O35042 TDS states only qualitatively, so chemical service life can be specified from the Haldia data and not from the Reliance data 2. It specifies the 240–280 °C oven temperature the roto process requires 3. Haldia is NOT better for diesel fuel tanks. O35042's octene chemistry gives No Break notched Izod and 950% elongation @ break for hydrocarbon-contact toughness; 73204T is a butene grade with no fuel-contact or permeation qualification in its TDS. For diesel tanks there is no technically suitable Haldia alternative in the supplied range
competition.alt_note: 73204T (closest available — butene grade)

desc: Relene X24065, is a Butene co-monomer based Linear Low Density Polyethylene. This grade is
designed for XLPE (silane grafted) cable compounds. It offers superior Processability, ESCR and
Abrasion resistance.
uses: Medium voltage XLPE cable compounding application

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 6.4 g/10 min 2. Density 0.924 g/cm³ 3. Tensile Stress @ Yield 11 MPa 4. Tensile Strength @ Break 15 MPa 5. Elongation @ Yield 17% 6. Elongation @ Break >600% 7. Flexural Modulus 260 MPa 8. Hardness Shore D 53
competition.superior: Designed for silane grafted XLPE cable compounds with superior processability, ESCR and abrasion resistance.
competition.limitations: 1. ESCR and abrasion resistance quoted qualitatively — no numerical values in the TDS 2. Dielectric strength, volume resistivity and cleanliness data Not available in official TDS 3. Properties before cross-linking are low (Flexural Modulus 260 MPa) — performance depends entirely on the cure step
competition.haldia_alt: No technically suitable Haldia grade in the supplied range
competition.comparison: 1. Haldia's supplied portfolio contains no wire and cable base resin for cross-linkable compounds 2. The only cable-related Haldia grade is E5201, a HDPE recommended for cable sheathing and jacketing compound — an outer protective layer, not a cross-linkable insulation base 3. E5201 at 0.950 g/cm³ and Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa is roughly four times the stiffness of the 260 MPa X24065 requires
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia is NOT better — it has no equivalent. Sheathing and cross-linked insulation are distinct functions with distinct qualification requirements, and E5201's TDS makes no silane-grafting or dielectric claim 2. Substituting a HDPE sheathing resin into a medium voltage insulation compound is an electrical-safety issue, not a performance trade-off 3. For medium voltage XLPE cable compounding there is no technically suitable Haldia alternative in the supplied range

desc: Relpure 5401P is a random copolymer polypropylene grade with low melt flow, offering excellent
processability, good clarity and impact resistance. It is specifically designed for applications in blow
molding and extrusion. Relpure 5401P is well-suited for pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food-contact
products and is also suitable for medical application.
uses: BFS IV Bottles, ISBM IV Bottles, Cosmetic containers and Food Containers

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 1.9 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 g/cc 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 26 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 12% 5. Flexural Modulus 800 MPa 6. Notched Izod Impact 65 J/m 7. HDT (455 KPa) 90 °C 8. Hardness Shore D 67
competition.superior: Random copolymer at low melt flow, giving the melt strength, clarity and impact resistance required for Blow Fill Seal pharmaceutical bottles.
competition.limitations: 1. Low stiffness (Flexural Modulus 800 MPa) — not for rigid load-bearing containers 2. HDT 90 °C — verify before any steam sterilisation duty 3. Haze and clarity values Not available in official TDS despite the clarity positioning
competition.comparison: 1. Direct match on polymer class, flow and duty — B202S is Haldia's PP random copolymer for blow moulded bottles and containers for medical applications and transparent products, at MFR 1.9 g/10 min, identical to 5401P 2. Haldia B202S is stronger at yield (27 MPa vs 26 MPa), stiffer (Flexural Modulus 900 MPa vs 800 MPa) and substantially tougher (Notched Izod 90 J/m vs 65 J/m) 3. Reliance 5401P has the higher HDT (90 °C vs 68 °C for B202S)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia B202S delivers 38% higher notched Izod (90 J/m vs 65 J/m) at identical MFR, which for thin-walled IV and pharmaceutical bottles means better resistance to cracking on drop and during handling of filled units 2. It is explicitly specified for excellent Melt Strength, High Clarity and Gloss and is named for medical application bottles, and its 900 MPa stiffness against 800 MPa gives better bottle top-load and shape retention 3. Its declared die temperature of 190–210 °C with barrel 160–210 °C is a blow-moulding specific profile, against a single 180–240 °C melt band for 5401P 4. Trade-off: 5401P's HDT of 90 °C against 68 °C is a real advantage where filled containers face warm storage or a hot-fill step, so B202S should not be substituted into hot-fill duty without verification

desc: Repol AM120N is PP homopolymer grade recommended for Injection Molding. It is an ideal choice
for general purpose injection molding and suitable for making furniture compounds.

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 12 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 g/cc 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 37 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 12% 5. Flexural Modulus 1450 MPa 6. Notched Izod Impact 30 J/m 7. HDT (455 KPa) 105 °C 8. Hardness Shore D 70
competition.superior: High tensile strength (37 MPa) at medium-high flow, making it an ideal general purpose injection grade that also serves as a furniture compound base.
competition.limitations: 1. Low impact strength (Notched Izod 30 J/m) — unsuitable for drop-critical or cold-service parts 2. Homopolymer — no low temperature toughness 3. Vicat Softening Point and ESCR Not available in official TDS
competition.comparison: 1. Direct match on flow and duty — M110 is a PP homopolymer at MFR 11 g/10 min recommended for injection moulded furniture and household items, against 12 g/10 min for AM120N 2. Haldia M110 is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1500 MPa vs 1450 MPa); Reliance AM120N is stronger at yield (37 MPa vs 34 MPa) and has higher HDT (105 °C vs 99 °C) 3. Notched Izod is comparable (30 J/m for both)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia M110's 1500 MPa flexural modulus against 1450 MPa gives marginally better panel rigidity in furniture sections, and it is specified for Low Cycle Time, High Gloss and Excellent Colour — the finish attributes that matter for visible furniture parts 2. Its declared barrel range of 180–280 °C is wider than the 210–260 °C of AM120N, giving more latitude on multi-zone tooling 3. Trade-off: Haldia is not better on strength or heat. AM120N's 37 MPa yield strength and 105 °C HDT against 34 MPa and 99 °C make it the better choice for load-bearing industrial mouldings and for parts stored or transported in hot conditions

desc: Repol AM650N is PP homopolymer grade recommended for use in Injection Molding. It is a
material of choice for use in Compounding / Masterbatch.
uses: TWIM containers, Articles with intricate long flow paths and Multicavity molding, Compounding & Masterbatch Manufacturing

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 65 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 g/cc 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 35 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 12% 5. Flexural Modulus 1350 MPa 6. Notched Izod Impact 25 J/m 7. HDT (455 KPa) 105 °C 8. Hardness Shore D 70
competition.superior: Very high flow (MFR 65) at homopolymer stiffness, filling articles with intricate long flow paths and multi-cavity tools, and serving as a compounding and masterbatch base.
competition.limitations: 1. Very low impact strength (Notched Izod 25 J/m) — brittle in drop and cold service 2. High flow reduces melt strength — unsuitable for extrusion or blow moulding 3. Vicat Softening Point and ESCR Not available in official TDS
competition.haldia_alt: M365 (closest available — impact copolymer, not homopolymer)
competition.comparison: 1. Flow is very closely matched — M365 at MFR 65 g/10 min is identical to AM650N, and both are positioned for thin wall injection moulding and compounding 2. The polymer class differs: M365 is a nucleated heterophasic impact copolymer, AM650N is a homopolymer 3. Reliance AM650N is far stronger and stiffer (Tensile @ Yield 35 MPa vs 22 MPa; Flexural Modulus 1350 MPa vs 1200 MPa); Haldia M365 is far tougher (Notched Izod 75 J/m vs 25 J/m) and higher in Vicat (148 °C)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia M365 delivers three times the notched Izod (75 J/m vs 25 J/m) at identical MFR 65, which for thin wall containers is the difference between a part that survives a drop test and one that shatters at the gate 2. Its nucleation gives low cycle time at the same flow, supporting multi-cavity productivity 3. Trade-off: this is a class substitution, not an equivalent. AM650N's 35 MPa yield strength against 22 MPa — a 59% advantage — and its homopolymer clarity and rigidity cannot be reproduced by an impact copolymer. Haldia has no homopolymer above MFR 35 (F135), so for high-flow homopolymer TWIM and masterbatch duty there is no true equivalent
competition.alt_note: M365 (closest available — impact copolymer, not homopolymer)

desc: Repol AS030N is a PP homopolymer grade recommended for raffia tapes used in plastics woven
sack. It exhibits good processability and excellent mechanical properties. The grade is designed
for low water carry over.
uses: Woven fabrics, Sacks & Monofilaments, Carpet backing, Industrial packaging and Geotextiles

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 3 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 g/cc 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 35 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 12% 5. Flexural Modulus 1400 MPa 6. Notched Izod Impact 44 J/m 7. HDT (455 KPa) 105 °C 8. Hardness Shore D 70
competition.superior: Good processability with excellent mechanical properties for raffia tape, carrying higher notched Izod (44 J/m) than typical homopolymer raffia grades.
competition.limitations: 1. Homopolymer — low temperature toughness is limited despite the 44 J/m Izod 2. No UV stabiliser stated — geotextile and outdoor fabric service requires an added UV package 3. Stretch ratio and oven temperature not specified in the TDS
competition.comparison: 1. Direct application match — R103 is Haldia's PP homopolymer for stretched tape raffia for woven sacks, FIBC, ropes and yarns, at MFR 3 g/10 min, identical to AS030N 2. Haldia R103 is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1500 MPa vs 1400 MPa) and higher in Vicat (153 °C); Reliance AS030N is stronger at yield (35 MPa vs 34 MPa) and tougher (Izod 44 J/m vs 40 J/m) 3. Both are positioned around low water carry-over for stable tape lines
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia R103's 1500 MPa flexural modulus against 1400 MPa raises tape stiffness at equal denier, which improves loom performance and sack body rigidity in filled cement and fertiliser bags 2. It specifies the complete raffia line — barrel 220–280 °C, die 260–280 °C, quench 30–40 °C and a ~160 °C oven stretching temperature — where the Reliance TDS omits the stretching oven setting entirely 3. Trade-off: AS030N carries higher notched Izod (44 J/m vs 40 J/m) and equal tensile, so for FIBC and heavy industrial sacks subject to drop loading the Reliance grade is marginally tougher

desc: Repol AS160N is PP homopolymer grade recommended for multifilament yarn and staple fiber. It
has excellent processability for production of high tenacity multifilament yarn.

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 16 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 g/cc 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 37 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 11% 5. Flexural Modulus 1500 MPa 6. Notched Izod Impact 25 J/m 7. HDT (455 KPa) 105 °C 8. Hardness Shore D 70
competition.superior: Excellent processability for high tenacity multifilament spinning, with the highest tensile strength (37 MPa) and stiffness (1500 MPa) in the Reliance fibre series.
competition.limitations: 1. Low impact strength (Notched Izod 25 J/m) — a fibre grade only, not for moulding 2. No gas fading stabiliser stated — may discolour in nonwoven and hygiene service 3. Vicat Softening Point Not available in official TDS
competition.comparison: 1. F135 is Haldia's only fibre and nonwoven grade — a controlled rheology homopolymer recommended for spunbond nonwoven and extrusion coating 2. There is a large flow gap: F135 runs at MFR 35 g/10 min against 16 g/10 min for AS160N, more than double 3. Reliance AS160N is stronger at yield (37 MPa vs 35 MPa) and stiffer (1500 MPa vs 1350 MPa); Haldia F135 is tougher (Izod 45 J/m vs 25 J/m) and has equal HDT (105 °C)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia F135 offers controlled rheology with narrow molecular weight distribution and declared gas fading resistance — the property that prevents yellowing in hygiene and medical nonwovens, which the AS160N TDS does not claim 2. Its 45 J/m notched Izod against 25 J/m gives more robust filament handling through godets and winders 3. Trade-off: the flow mismatch is the limiting factor. At MFR 35 against 16, F135 spins to finer denier but cannot reach the high tenacity that AS160N's lower MFR and 37 MPa tensile deliver. For high tenacity multifilament yarn, F135 is the closest available Haldia grade but is not a technical equivalent
competition.alt_note: F135 (closest available — significant flow gap)

desc: Repol AS12000N is an ultra-high melt flow, narrow molecular weight distribution polypropylene
homopolymer grade used for Melt Blown Non-Woven. High Melt Flow and Narrow MWD helps in
optimum processing / line speeds and can be melt blown in to ultra-fine denier fibers.
uses: Melt blown nonwoven fabrics for Absorption & Filtration, Hygiene & Medical Disposables, Masks, Wipes and others

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 1200 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 g/cc 3. DSC Melting Temperature 165 °C 4. Mechanical properties Not available in official TDS (ultra-high flow resin characterised by MFR and melting point)
competition.superior: Ultra-high melt flow (MFR 1200) with narrow molecular weight distribution — the specific rheology required to draw sub-micron fibres in melt blown dies.
competition.limitations: 1. Extremely high MFR gives essentially no melt strength — usable only on melt blown dies, not on any other process 2. Mechanical properties (tensile, flexural, impact) Not available in official TDS 3. Requires a high extrusion temperature of 260–290 °C with tight thermal control
competition.haldia_alt: No technically suitable Haldia grade in the supplied range
competition.comparison: 1. Haldia's supplied portfolio contains no melt blown grade; its highest flow PP is F135 at MFR 35 g/10 min 2. The rheology gap is roughly 34-fold (MFR 1200 vs 35), which no process adjustment can bridge — F135 would not attenuate into melt blown micro-fibres and would rope at the die 3. F135 is a spunbond grade, a fundamentally different web-forming process with different fibre diameters and bonding mechanisms
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia is NOT better — it has no equivalent. Melt blown requires a controlled rheology resin engineered specifically for MFR in the hundreds to low thousands; nothing in the supplied Haldia range approaches this 2. Haldia F135 serves spunbond nonwoven only, which is a complementary rather than substitutable web technology 3. For melt blown filtration media, masks and wipes there is no technically suitable Haldia alternative in the supplied range

desc: Repol H019TG is Polypropylene Homopolymer grade recommended for use in Extrusion & Blow
Molding applications. It is an ideal material to be used for strappings, stationery items etc.
uses: Sheets, strappings, tubing, blow molded containers, straws, ball pen refills, sheets and thermoformed containers

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 1.9 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 g/cc 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 35 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 8% 5. Flexural Modulus 1700 MPa 6. Notched Izod Impact 40 J/m 7. HDT (455 KPa) 105 °C 8. Hardness Shore D 70
competition.superior: Very high stiffness (1700 MPa) at low MFR (1.9), giving the melt strength needed for strapping, sheet and extrusion blow moulding in one grade.
competition.limitations: 1. Low MFR (1.9) — unsuitable for thin wall or multi-cavity injection moulding 2. Notched Izod 40 J/m — homopolymer toughness only, brittle below ambient 3. Vicat Softening Point Not available in official TDS
competition.comparison: 1. T103 is Haldia's PP homopolymer for thermoforming of cups, containers and disposable items, the closest match to H019TG's sheet and thermoforming duty 2. Flow differs: T103 at MFR 4 g/10 min against 1.9 g/10 min for H019TG, so Reliance has the higher melt strength 3. Haldia T103 is stronger at yield (37 MPa vs 35 MPa), tougher (Izod 60 J/m vs 40 J/m) and equally stiff (Flexural Modulus 1700 MPa for both)

Haldia T103 carries 50% higher notched Izod (60 J/m vs 40 J/m) at the same 1700 MPa stiffness, which reduces cracking of thin thermoformed cup rims and flanges during de-nesting 2. It specifies the sheet line directly — barrel 190–230 °C and die 220–250 °C — against a broad 170–250 °C melt band for H019TG 3. Trade-off: T103's MFR of 4 against 1.9 means less melt strength, so it is the weaker choice for extrusion blow moulded containers, strapping and tubing, where H019TG's lower flow holds the parison and profile. Haldia has no PP strapping or extrusion blow moulding homopolymer, so that part of the duty is uncovered

desc: plastic woven sack. It exhibits good processability and excellent mechanical properties. The grade is
formulated with additive package for low water carry over.
uses: Woven fabrics for FIBC, Geotextiles, Ropes, Monofilaments & carpet backing

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 2.6 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 g/cc 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 34 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 10% 5. Flexural Modulus 1700 MPa 6. Notched Izod Impact 40 J/m 7. HDT (455 KPa) 104 °C 8. Hardness Shore D 70

Flow is close: R103 at MFR 3 g/10 min against 2.6 g/10 min for H026SG 3. Reliance H026SG is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1700 MPa vs 1500 MPa); Haldia R103 is stronger at yield (34 MPa for both — equal) with Izod 40 J/m (equal) and Vicat 153 °C

Haldia R103 specifies the full raffia process chain including the ~160 °C oven stretching temperature and 260–280 °C die, which is the setting that determines achievable tape tenacity — the Reliance TDS gives extrusion and water bath temperatures but no stretching data 2. Its explicit FIBC, rope and yarn qualification matches H026SG's heavy duty fabric target directly 3. Honest trade-off: Haldia is NOT better on the property that matters most here. H026SG's 1700 MPa flexural modulus against 1500 MPa is a 13% stiffness advantage, and tape modulus is precisely what governs FIBC fabric rigidity and geotextile load spreading. desc: woven sack. It exhibits good processability and excellent mechanical properties. The grade is
designed for low water carry over.

competition.superior: High stiffness (1650 MPa) raffia grade at moderate flow, suited to general purpose woven sack and monofilament production.

Haldia R103 declares Vicat 153 °C and Elongation @ Yield 9% against 10% for Reliance

Haldia R103 publishes the complete stretched-tape process window — barrel 220–280 °C, die 260–280 °C, quench 30–40 °C and ~160 °C oven stretching — which allows a converter to commission a line without trial-and-error; H030SG omits the stretching temperature 2. desc: suitable for low thickness films and processing on high line speeds. It is the material of choice for
BOPP films used in adhesive tapes, food packaging, cigarette & textile overwraps, synthetic paper,

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 3.4 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 g/cc 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 36 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 12% 5. Flexural Modulus 1350 MPa 6. Notched Izod Impact 40 J/m 7. HDT (455 KPa) 104 °C 8. Hardness Shore D 69
competition.superior: Designed for oriented film lines with the high tensile (36 MPa) and controlled flow needed for plain and metallisable BOPP.
competition.limitations: 1. Dedicated BOPP grade — not suitable for injection moulding or blow moulding 2. Haze, gloss and optical data Not available in official TDS 3. Notched Izod 40 J/m — not for impact-loaded parts
competition.comparison: 1. Direct application match — F103 is Haldia's BOPP homopolymer for food packaging, lamination and metallisable applications, at MFR 3 g/10 min against 3.4 g/10 min for H034SG 2. Haldia F103 is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1450 MPa vs 1350 MPa) and higher in Vicat (152 °C); Reliance H034SG is stronger at yield (36 MPa vs 34 MPa) 3. Notched Izod is comparable (40 J/m for both)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia F103 is explicitly designed for stable extrusion on stenter lines with low water carryover and good thickness control — the three parameters that determine BOPP line uptime and gauge uniformity, stated as design targets rather than inferred 2. Its 1450 MPa flexural modulus against 1350 MPa gives a stiffer film at equal gauge, improving machinability on high speed packaging lines, and it declares Clarity, Gloss, Impact and Puncture Resistance — optical attributes the H034SG TDS omits entirely 3. Its specified water bath temperature of 10–15 °C with barrel at 230–280 °C is a tighter, BOPP-specific casting window than the 20–50 °C chill roll range given by Reliance 4. Trade-off: H034SG has the higher yield strength (36 MPa vs 34 MPa), which marginally favours very thin gauge tape film

desc: Repol H045SG is PP homopolymer grade recommended for making raffia tapes used in making
plastic woven sack. The grade is designed for high speed processing on tape lines and ideal
material for low denier raffia tapes. It is formulated with additive package for low water carry over.

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 4.5 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 g/cc 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 32 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 8% 5. Flexural Modulus 1350 MPa 6. Notched Izod Impact 30 J/m 7. HDT (455 KPa) 104 °C 8. Hardness Shore D 70
competition.superior: Higher flow (MFR 4.5) designed for high speed processing of low weight general purpose wrapping fabric.

Flow differs: R103 at MFR 3 g/10 min against 4.5 g/10 min for H045SG, so Reliance is the higher speed grade 3. Haldia R103 is substantially stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1500 MPa vs 1350 MPa), stronger at yield (34 MPa vs 32 MPa) and tougher (Izod 40 J/m vs 30 J/m)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia R103 outperforms H045SG on every mechanical measure — 1500 MPa vs 1350 MPa stiffness, 34 MPa vs 32 MPa tensile and 40 J/m vs 30 J/m impact — so tape of equal denier carries more load and resists splitting better in the loom 2. It publishes the ~160 °C oven stretching temperature that governs tape tenacity, absent from the Reliance TDS 3. Trade-off: R103's lower MFR (3 vs 4.5) means lower line speed and higher extruder load. H045SG is specifically designed for high speed processing of low weight wrapping fabric, so where output rate rather than tape strength is the constraint, the Reliance grade is the more productive choice
