desc: High Density Polyethylene HDPE B55H02 is a natural colored grade produced with the latest Mitsui CX slurry polymerization Technology exhibiting following features:  High Impact Strength  Rigidity  Low Parison Sag  Good ESCR Properties
uses: Large volume containers for transport & storage of Chemicals

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/5.00 kg) 0.20 g/10 min 2. MFI (190°C/21.6 kg) 5.00 g/10 min 3. Density 0.955 gm/cm³ 4. Tensile Strength @ Yield 28 MPa 5. Notched Izod Impact 500 J/m; Charpy NB 6. Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa 7. ESCR (F50) >600 hrs 8. Vicat 125 °C; HDT 80 °C; Tm 132 °C
competition.superior: Mitsui CX slurry HMHDPE combining 500 J/m notched Izod with No Break Charpy and low parison sag at MFI5 0.20 — the melt strength needed for very large accumulator-head containers.
competition.limitations: 1. Very low MFI (0.20 g/10 min @ 5 kg) requires accumulator-head equipment — not for small or thin-wall containers 2. ESCR >600 hrs is moderate for aggressive surfactant or pesticide contents 3. Supplied natural with no UV stabiliser — external UV masterbatch needed for outdoor tanks 4. Issued as a Provisional Technical Datasheet; values may change
competition.comparison: 1. Direct application match — B5500 is Haldia's HMHDPE blow moulding grade for medium bulk containers (~120 litre) for chemicals, detergent and lube oils, the same contents B55H02 targets 2. Notched Izod is identical at 500 J/m and flexural modulus identical at 1000 MPa; density is close (0.952 vs 0.955 gm/cm³) 3. Haldia B5500 runs at higher flow (MFI5 0.35 vs 0.20 g/10 min) and declares higher ESCR (>1000 hrs vs >600 hrs) and higher tensile @ yield (27 MPa — OPaL is higher at 28 MPa)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia B5500 declares ESCR >1000 hrs against >600 hrs — for detergent, surfactant and chemical drums stress-crack life is the property that sets service life, and a 1.7-fold margin is a real durability difference 2. Its higher MFI5 (0.35 vs 0.20 g/10 min) lowers melt pressure and motor load at equal output, and it publishes a full blow-moulding profile (barrel 200/210/215/210 °C, die 200–210 °C, parison 190–210 °C, mould water 20–25 °C) against a single 180–220 °C band from OPaL 3. Trade-off: B55H02's lower MFI gives better parison hold on the largest parts, and its 28 MPa yield strength slightly exceeds B5500's 27 MPa. For containers well above 120 litres the OPaL grade has the better melt strength

desc: High Density Polyethylene HDPE B55H03 is a natural colored grade produced with the latest Mitsui CX slurry polymerization Technology exhibiting following features:  High Impact Strength  Rigidity  Low Parison Sag  Good ESCR Properties
uses: Large Containers (up to 100L) for transport & storage of Chemicals

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/5.00 kg) 0.35 g/10 min 2. MFI (190°C/21.6 kg) 9.00 g/10 min 3. Density 0.955 gm/cm³ 4. Tensile Strength @ Yield 28 MPa; @ Break 40 MPa 5. Notched Izod Impact 500 J/m; Charpy NB 6. Flexural Modulus 1000 MPa 7. ESCR (F50) >600 hrs 8. Vicat 129 °C; HDT 80 °C
competition.superior: Higher flow version of the B55 series (MFI5 0.35) holding 500 J/m impact and 40 MPa break strength, with a Vicat of 129 °C — the highest of the OPaL blow moulding range.
competition.limitations: 1. ESCR >600 hrs limits use with highly aggressive chemicals 2. No UV stabiliser stated — water tanks in outdoor service require an added UV package 3. Issued as a Provisional Technical Datasheet; values may change
competition.comparison: 1. Closest pairing in the whole comparison — B5500 is qualified for ~120 L bulk containers for chemicals, detergent and lube oils AND for blow moulded water tanks up to 1000 litres, matching both stated applications of B55H03 2. Melt flow is identical (MFI5 0.35 g/10 min for both); Izod identical at 500 J/m; flexural modulus identical at 1000 MPa; tensile @ break identical at 40 MPa 3. Haldia B5500 declares ESCR >1000 hrs against >600 hrs; OPaL B55H03 has the higher tensile @ yield (28 MPa vs 27 MPa) and Vicat (129 °C vs 127 °C)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. At matched flow, stiffness, impact and break strength, the deciding property is ESCR, and Haldia B5500's >1000 hrs against >600 hrs gives a materially longer stress-crack life for detergent and chemical drums 2. B5500 states explicitly that adequate UV stabiliser must be added externally for outdoor water tank use — the same requirement applies to B55H03 but is not stated, so the Haldia TDS gives clearer processing guidance for the 1000 L tank application 3. Trade-off: B55H03's Vicat of 129 °C against 127 °C gives slightly better resistance to warm-warehouse stacking deformation, and its 28 MPa yield strength is marginally higher. These two grades are close to interchangeable

Flexural modulus is identical at 1300 MPa, tensile @ yield identical at 32 MPa, density close (0.960 vs 0.962 gm/cm³) and Vicat identical at 129 °C 3. competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia B6401 publishes an ESCR figure (<20 hrs) where B6003 publishes none. That low value is honest disclosure rather than a weakness for this duty — it correctly signals that neither grade should be used for detergent or surfactant contents, a limit a buyer cannot establish from the B6003 TDS at all 2. B6401 declares tensile strength @ break of 40 MPa and publishes a full blow profile (barrel 150/160/165/175 °C, die 180–185 °C, parison 185–190 °C, mould water 20–25 °C), where OPaL gives one 160–200 °C band and no break strength 3. OPaL R5410 covers tape and cordage in one grade; Haldia splits the duty — HD T9 for stretched tape / raffia for woven fabrics and tarpaulin, HD T10 for yarns and monofilament for fabrics, nets, twines and ropes 2. Haldia grades run at higher flow (MFI 1.1 vs 0.90 g/10 min @ 2.16 kg) at lower density (0.950 vs 0.954 gm/cm³) 3. Haldia HD T9 / HD T10 declare Notched Izod 400 J/m against 250 J/m, Tensile @ Break 38 MPa against 35 MPa, Elongation @ Break 1100% against >500%, Flexural Modulus 1100 / 1000 MPa against 850 MPa and Vicat 127 °C against 122 °C

Haldia HD T9 and HD T10 exceed R5410 on every published tape-relevant property — 38 MPa break strength against 35 MPa, 400 J/m impact against 250 J/m, 1100 MPa flexural modulus against 850 MPa and 1100% elongation against >500% — so tape of equal denier carries more load and tolerates a higher stretch ratio before fibrillation 2. They publish the complete stretch-line setup that determines achievable tenacity: barrel 200–240 °C, die 230–250 °C, quench 30 °C and, for HD T10, a 95–120 °C stretching temperature. The R5410 TDS gives only a 200–240 °C extrusion band with no die, quench or stretch data 3. Trade-off: two Haldia grades are needed to replace one OPaL grade, so a converter running tape and nets on shared silos loses the single-resin simplicity R5410 offers. Haldia R5801 is an alternative tape grade at higher density (0.960) and stiffness (1150 MPa) if maximum fabric rigidity is the target

Flow is close (MFI 1.1 vs 0.90 g/10 min @ 2.16 kg); Haldia runs at lower density (0.950 vs 0.957 gm/cm³) 3. Haldia HD T10S declares Tensile @ Yield 26 MPa against 24 MPa, @ Break 38 MPa against 35 MPa, Notched Izod 400 J/m against 120 J/m, Elongation @ Break 1100% against >500% and Vicat 127 °C against 122 °C; OPaL Y5710 is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 950 MPa vs 1000 MPa — Haldia is in fact stiffer)

For drip laterals Haldia 71601D is the technically correct choice rather than 71601W: it is additivated specifically for that duty and declares ESCR 1000 hrs and 30 MPa break strength, data F2001A does not provide for its stated drip lateral use 4. Trade-off: F2001A's 44 MPa MD tensile at break against 25 MPa is a 76% advantage and is decisive for stretch and heavy-duty lamination film. Note the film test bases differ (OPaL 40 µ at 2.25 BUR; Haldia 25 µ at 2.5 BUR), so the comparison is directional

desc: Linear Low Density Polyethylene LLDPE M2525 is a butene co-monomer based linear low density grade produced with the latest Ineos Gas Phase polymerization Technology exhibiting following features:  Excellent Flow & Processability  Good warpage resistance.

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 25.0 g/10 min 2. Density 0.934 gm/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 12 MPa 4. Elongation @ Break >500% 5. Flexural Modulus 250 MPa 6. Vicat 95 °C
competition.superior: High flow (MFI 25) with good warpage resistance, giving fast cycles on thin-wall lids and clean dispersion as a masterbatch carrier.
competition.limitations: 1. Very low stiffness (Flexural Modulus 250 MPa) — not for structural or load-bearing parts 2. Vicat 95 °C limits warm service and hot-fill use 3. Notched Izod and ESCR are Not available in official TDS 4. Issued as a Provisional Technical Datasheet; values may change
competition.haldia_alt: No technically suitable Haldia grade in the supplied range (M5018L is the nearest injection grade)
competition.comparison: 1. Haldia's supplied portfolio contains no LLDPE injection moulding or masterbatch grade — all its LLDPE grades are film, drip lateral, extrusion coating or rotational moulding 2. M5018L matches approximately on flow (MFI 20 against 25 g/10 min) but is HDPE at 0.950 gm/cm³ with Flexural Modulus 800 MPa and Vicat 121 °C, against 0.934 gm/cm³, 250 MPa and 95 °C for M2525 3. The stiffness difference is more than three-fold, which is a material-class difference rather than a grade difference
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia is NOT better — it has no equivalent. A masterbatch carrier must melt below the host polymer and disperse pigment without stiffening the article, which M2525's 95 °C Vicat and 250 MPa modulus deliver and M5018L's 121 °C Vicat and 800 MPa modulus do not 2. Substituting M5018L into flexible lids and thin-wall containers would give rigid parts that crack rather than flex at the closure 3. M5018L is a valid alternative only for rigid general purpose housewares and HDPE-host masterbatch, not for LLDPE or LDPE-host masterbatch or flexible lid moulding
competition.alt_note: No technically suitable Haldia grade in the supplied range (M5018L is the nearest injection grade)

desc: Linear Low Density Polyethylene LLDPE T3804 is a butene co-monomer based medium density grade produced with the latest Ineos Gas Phase polymerization Technology exhibiting following features:  Excellent Processability  High Stiffness & Impact Strength  Excellent Internal & External Surface finish

competition.key_props: 1. MFI (190°C/2.16 kg) 4.0 g/10 min 2. Density 0.938 gm/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 15 MPa 4. Elongation @ Break >500% 5. Flexural Modulus 280 MPa 6. Notched Izod 650 J/m 7. ESCR (F50) 200 hrs 8. Vicat 117 °C
competition.superior: The highest notched Izod in the OPaL range (650 J/m) at medium density, with excellent internal and external surface finish for roto moulded tanks.
competition.limitations: 1. No UV stabiliser — carbon black or UV masterbatch blending required for continuous outdoor exposure 2. Low stiffness (Flexural Modulus 280 MPa) limits unsupported tank span 3. Oven cycle and peak internal air temperature are Not available in official TDS 4. Issued as a Provisional Technical Datasheet; values may change
competition.comparison: 1. Direct application match — 73005T is Haldia's LLDPE roto moulding grade ideally suited to tanks and containers for domestic and industrial water storage, sanitation and agriculture, the same application list as T3804 2. Flow is close (MFI 5.0 vs 4.0 g/10 min); Haldia runs at lower density (0.934 vs 0.938 gm/cm³) 3. Haldia 73005T is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 400 MPa against 280 MPa), stronger at yield (17 MPa against 15 MPa) and higher in Vicat (110 °C — OPaL is higher at 117 °C); OPaL T3804 is far tougher (Izod 650 J/m against 350 J/m) and higher in ESCR (200 hrs against 100 hrs)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia 73005T's 400 MPa flexural modulus against 280 MPa is a 43% stiffness gain, which for a large overhead tank is the property that resists wall bulging under head pressure and therefore sets wall thickness — the dominant design constraint in roto moulding 2. It specifies the oven temperature of 240–280 °C that the rotational moulding process is actually set to, where the OPaL TDS quotes a 180–230 °C melt-processing band that is not a usable oven setting for this process 3. Honest trade-off: Haldia is NOT better on durability. T3804 carries 650 J/m notched Izod against 350 J/m and double the ESCR (200 hrs against 100 hrs), plus a higher Vicat (117 °C against 110 °C). Where impact and stress-crack life govern, the OPaL grade is stronger; Haldia 73204T (Izod 500 J/m, ESCR 500 hrs) is the better Haldia selection if ESCR is the critical property

Flow is close (MFI 5.0 vs 4.0 g/10 min); Haldia is lower in density (0.934 vs 0.938 gm/cm³) 3. Haldia 73005TU is stiffer (400 MPa against 280 MPa), stronger at yield (17 MPa against 15 MPa) and declares Elongation @ Break 800%; OPaL T3804U is far tougher (Izod 650 J/m against 350 J/m), higher in ESCR (200 hrs against 100 hrs) and Vicat (117 °C against 110 °C)

Haldia 73005TU names its stabiliser system — Light Stabilizer + — and ties it explicitly to long service life under outdoor exposure, where T3804U states UV (HALS) Stabilized with no loading or service-life figure; for tanks and traffic barriers in permanent sun that is the difference between a verifiable and an unverifiable weathering specification 2. Its 400 MPa flexural modulus against 280 MPa gives materially better wall rigidity under head pressure, and it specifies the 240–280 °C oven temperature the process requires 3. Honest trade-off: T3804U is the tougher and more stress-crack resistant resin — 650 J/m against 350 J/m and 200 hrs ESCR against 100 hrs. Haldia 73204TU (Izod 500 J/m, ESCR 500 hrs, also Light Stabilizer +) is the better Haldia choice where chemical or chlorinated water contact drives the design

desc: Polypropylene Homo Polymer PP Homo polymer FH10S is a natural colored high stiffness grade produced with the latest Ineos Gas Phase polymerization Technology exhibiting following features:  Higher flow for easy processing.  High Stiffness.  Excellent gloss & clarity of films  With Slip & Antiblock additives

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 10 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 gm/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 35 MPa 4. Elongation @ Break 30% 5. Flexural Modulus 1500 MPa 6. Notch Izod Impact 25 J/m 7. Hardness Rockwell R 95 8. HDT (0.46 N/mm²) 100 °C; contains slip and antiblock
competition.superior: High stiffness homopolymer (1500 MPa) with excellent gloss and clarity, slip and antiblock additivated for tubular water quenched film.
competition.limitations: 1. Recommended processing temperature is Not available in official TDS — no processing window is published at all 2. Vicat Softening Point is Not available in official TDS 3. Haze, gloss and COF are Not available in official TDS despite the clarity and gloss claim 4. Low impact (25 J/m); requires a water quench ring and is not usable on air-cooled blown film lines 5. Issued as a Provisional Technical Datasheet; values may change
competition.comparison: 1. Direct process and additive match — F110 is Haldia's PP homopolymer recommended for Tubular Quenched (TQ) film for packaging foodstuffs and garments, and like FH10S it contains slip and antiblocking additives for openability 2. Melt flow is closely matched at MFR 11 vs 10 g/10 min, at identical density (0.90) 3. OPaL FH10S is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1500 MPa against 1400 MPa) and marginally higher in HDT (100 °C against 99 °C); Haldia F110 is tougher (Izod 30 J/m against 25 J/m), stronger at yield (34 MPa — OPaL is higher at 35 MPa) and declares Vicat 154 °C
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia F110 publishes a complete processing window — barrel 180–230 °C with die 190–210 °C — where the FH10S TDS gives no recommended processing temperature at all. For a water-quenched film line, where bubble stability depends on tight die control, that omission alone makes the Haldia grade the more usable specification 2. It declares Vicat 154 °C, giving a heat-seal and softening reference that FH10S omits, and its 30 J/m notched Izod against 25 J/m reduces film cracking at fold lines in bread and grocery bags 3. Trade-off: FH10S's 1500 MPa flexural modulus against 1400 MPa gives a stiffer, crisper film at equal gauge, which suits textile overwrap and snack packaging where film body is preferred over toughness

desc: Polypropylene Homo Polymer PP Homo polymer MH13 is a natural colored high stiffness grade produced with the latest Ineos Gas Phase polymerization Technology exhibiting following features:  Higher flow for easy processing.  High Stiffness.  Good dimensional stability  Faster Molding cycle

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 13.5 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 gm/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 34 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 6% 5. Flexural Modulus 1150 MPa 6. Notch Izod Impact 20 J/m 7. Hardness Rockwell R 95 8. Vicat 150 °C; HDT (0.46 N/mm²) 100 °C
competition.superior: High flow homopolymer (MFR 13.5) with good dimensional stability for faster moulding cycles on household and rigid packaging tools.
competition.limitations: 1. Recommended processing temperature is Not available in official TDS 2. Lowest notched Izod of the OPaL PP injection range (20 J/m) — brittle in drop service 3. Lowest flexural modulus of the OPaL PP injection grades (1150 MPa) 4. Issued as a Provisional Technical Datasheet; values may change
competition.comparison: 1. Direct match on class and duty — M110 is Haldia's PP homopolymer recommended for injection moulded furniture and household items, at MFR 11 vs 13.5 g/10 min and identical density 2. Haldia M110 is substantially stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1500 MPa against 1150 MPa), tougher (Izod 30 J/m against 20 J/m) and higher in Vicat (154 °C against 150 °C) 3. OPaL MH13 has the higher flow (13.5 against 11 g/10 min), marginally higher tensile @ yield (34 MPa for both — equal) and HDT (100 °C against 99 °C)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia M110's 1500 MPa flexural modulus against 1150 MPa is a 30% stiffness advantage, which for rigid packaging and houseware panels is the property that sets wall thickness and allows genuine down-gauging 2. Its 50% higher notched Izod (30 J/m against 20 J/m) meaningfully reduces gate-area and rim cracking in thin household mouldings, and it publishes a barrel range of 180–280 °C with mould 30–40 °C where MH13 publishes no processing window at all 3. It is specified for Low Cycle Time, High Gloss and Excellent Colour with a declared Vicat of 154 °C, giving both a finish specification and a softening reference 4. Trade-off: MH13's higher flow (13.5 against 11) fills long or thin flow paths at lower injection pressure, so for multi-cavity consumer-product tools the OPaL grade is the easier resin to run

desc: Polypropylene Homo Polymer PP Homo polymer MH13A is a natural colored high stiffness grade produced with the latest Ineos Gas Phase polymerization Technology exhibiting following features:  Higher flow for easy processing.  High Stiffness.  Good dimensional stability  Anti-Static Property

competition.superior: Antistatic-formulated high stiffness homopolymer (1400 MPa) at MFR 12, reducing static charge build-up on furniture and rigid packaging parts.
competition.limitations: 1. Recommended processing temperature is Not available in official TDS 2. Low impact strength (25 J/m) — homopolymer toughness only, brittle below ambient 3. Antistatic agent loading and surface resistivity are Not available in official TDS 4. Issued as a Provisional Technical Datasheet; values may change

competition.comparison: 1. M110 is Haldia's PP homopolymer for injection moulded furniture and household items, the closest match on class and duty, at MFR 11 vs 12 g/10 min and identical density 2. Haldia M110 is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1500 MPa against 1400 MPa), tougher (Izod 30 J/m against 25 J/m) and higher in Vicat (154 °C against 150 °C); OPaL MH13A is stronger at yield (35 MPa against 34 MPa) 3. Haldia's supplied portfolio contains no antistatic-formulated PP homopolymer
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia M110 leads on the two properties that govern furniture panels — 1500 MPa stiffness against 1400 MPa and 30 J/m impact against 25 J/m — and is specified for Low Cycle Time, High Gloss and Excellent Colour, with a published barrel range of 180–280 °C against no processing window from OPaL 2. Haldia is NOT better on the defining feature. MH13A's antistatic agent is the reason the grade exists, preventing dust pickup on furniture surfaces and charge build-up during compounding, and no Haldia PP grade in the supplied range carries an antistatic package 3. M110 is therefore the correct substitution for general furniture and rigid packaging duty, but an external antistatic masterbatch would have to be added to match MH13A's function
competition.alt_note: M110 (closest available — no antistatic grade in the Haldia range)

competition.comparison: 1. Direct application match — R103 is Haldia's PP homopolymer for stretched tape raffia for woven sacks, FIBC, ropes and yarns, covering the same cement, fertiliser and bulk packaging duty, at MFR 3 vs 3.3 g/10 min 2. Both are positioned around low water carry-over for stable tape lines; Vicat is close (153 °C vs 150 °C) and HDT close (93 °C vs 95 °C) 3. Haldia R103 is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1500 MPa against 1350 MPa) and equal at yield (34 MPa vs 35 MPa for OPaL — OPaL marginally higher); OPaL RH03 is tougher (Izod 44 J/m against 40 J/m)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia R103's 1500 MPa flexural modulus against 1350 MPa is an 11% tape-stiffness advantage, and tape modulus is precisely what governs woven fabric rigidity in filled cement and fertiliser sacks and load spreading in FIBC 2. It publishes the complete raffia chain — barrel 220–280 °C, die 260–280 °C, quench 30–40 °C and a ~160 °C oven stretching temperature. The stretching temperature is the setting that determines achievable tape tenacity, and the RH03 TDS omits it entirely 3. Trade-off: RH03 carries higher notched Izod (44 J/m against 40 J/m) and marginally higher yield strength (35 MPa against 34 MPa), so for drop-loaded industrial sacks it is the slightly tougher tape. The two grades are close and the choice is largely commercial

desc: Polypropylene Homo Polymer PP Homo polymer RH25X is a natural colored high performance grade produced with the latest Ineos Gas Phase polymerization Technology exhibiting following features:  Excellent Processability & strength  Very good resin purity & uniformity  Anti-gas fading properties

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 25 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 gm/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 35 MPa 4. Elongation @ Break 20% 5. Flexural Modulus 1450 MPa 6. Notch Izod Impact 20 J/m 7. Hardness Rockwell R 95 8. HDT (0.46 N/mm²) 100 °C; anti-gas fading
competition.superior: Very good resin purity and uniformity with anti-gas fading properties, formulated for fine denier spinning at high speed.
competition.limitations: 1. Recommended processing temperature is Not available in official TDS 2. Vicat Softening Point is Not available in official TDS 3. Low impact (20 J/m) — a fibre grade only, not for moulding 4. Quenching temperature, godet and draw ratio settings are Not available in official TDS 5. Issued as a Provisional Technical Datasheet; values may change
competition.comparison: 1. F135 is Haldia's only fibre and nonwoven grade — a controlled rheology homopolymer with declared gas fading resistance, matching RH25X's anti-gas fading positioning and spunbond application 2. There is a real flow gap: F135 runs at MFR 35 g/10 min against 25 for RH25X 3. Haldia F135 is more than twice as tough (Izod 45 J/m against 20 J/m), higher in HDT (105 °C against 100 °C) and declares Vicat 150 °C; OPaL RH25X is stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1450 MPa against 1350 MPa)
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia F135 is a controlled rheology resin with narrow molecular weight distribution, which produces more uniform fibre diameter at high spinning speed than a reactor-grade homopolymer, and it publishes barrel 180–220 °C with die 215–220 °C where RH25X publishes no processing window at all 2. Its 45 J/m notched Izod against 20 J/m more than doubles filament robustness through drawing, winding and calender bonding, and its declared Vicat of 150 °C and HDT of 105 °C give a fuller thermal dataset 3. Trade-off: the 40% flow gap matters. At MFR 35 against 25, F135 spins finer denier but cannot reach the tenacity that RH25X's lower melt flow and 1450 MPa stiffness support in multifilament yarn. F135 is the closest available Haldia grade rather than a technical equivalent for high tenacity yarn
competition.alt_note: F135 (closest available — significant flow gap)

desc: Polypropylene Homo Polymer PP Homo polymer RH38 is a natural colored high performance grade produced with the latest Ineos Gas Phase polymerization Technology exhibiting following features:  High Melt flow  Excellent Processability  Very good resin purity & uniformity

competition.key_props: 1. MFR (230°C/2.16 kg) 38 g/10 min 2. Density 0.90 gm/cm³ 3. Tensile Strength @ Yield 31 MPa 4. Elongation @ Yield 6.5% 5. Flexural Modulus 1085 MPa 6. Notch Izod Impact 20 J/m 7. Hardness Rockwell R 95 8. HDT (0.46 N/mm²) 100 °C; anti-gas fading
competition.superior: High melt flow (MFR 38) with very good resin purity, uniformity and anti-gas fading, designed for high speed spinning of fine denier fibre.
competition.limitations: 1. Recommended processing temperature is Not available in official TDS 2. Vicat Softening Point is Not available in official TDS 3. Lowest tensile @ yield (31 MPa) and flexural modulus (1085 MPa) of the OPaL PP range 4. Low impact (20 J/m) — a fibre grade only 5. Issued as a Provisional Technical Datasheet; values may change
competition.comparison: 1. Direct application match at close flow — F135 is Haldia's controlled rheology homopolymer recommended for spunbond nonwoven and suitable for hygiene products, at MFR 35 vs 38 g/10 min for RH38, and both declare gas fading resistance 2. Haldia F135 is stronger at yield (35 MPa against 31 MPa), stiffer (Flexural Modulus 1350 MPa against 1085 MPa), more than twice as tough (Izod 45 J/m against 20 J/m) and higher in HDT (105 °C against 100 °C) 3. Haldia F135 declares Vicat 150 °C, which RH38 omits, and adds extrusion coating on woven fabrics to the same grade's application list
competition.reason_haldia_better: 1. Haldia F135 leads on every published mechanical property at closely matched flow — 35 MPa yield against 31 MPa, 1350 MPa stiffness against 1085 MPa and 45 J/m impact against 20 J/m — so the spunbond web is both firmer and far more resistant to filament breakage during calender bonding 2. It publishes barrel 180–220 °C with die 215–220 °C, a fibre-line profile, where the RH38 TDS gives no processing window at all — a significant gap for a grade whose entire value depends on tight denier control 3. Its controlled rheology and narrow molecular weight distribution give more uniform fibre diameter at high spinning speed than a reactor-grade resin of the same nominal MFR 4. Trade-off: RH38's higher MFR (38 against 35) gives marginally finer attenuation at the same die pressure, and both grades share the gas fading resistance needed for hygiene nonwovens

competition_notes: 1.0 No Haldia LDPE in portfolio All 15 Reliance LDPE grades (16MA400, 22FA002, 24FS040, 1005FY20, 1020FA20, 1070LA17, J22FA002E, J24FA040, J24FS040, J1005FS20, J1005FY20, J1007FA20, J1020FA20, J1020FF20, J1020XA20) The supplied Haldia TDS set contains no LDPE grade. Every LDPE row is therefore matched to the closest LLDPE (or, for masterbatch, HDPE) grade and the polymer-class change is stated in the row. Shrink film, foam and LDPE-host masterbatch cannot be substituted at all.

2.0 No wire & cable resin in Haldia portfolio J1020XA20, X24065, and the W&C half of JF18020 and JF18030 Haldia supplies no cross-linkable insulation or W&C compound base resin. E5201 is a HDPE cable sheathing/jacketing grade — a different function — so it was NOT offered as a substitute. Marked 'No technically suitable Haldia grade'.

3.0 No octene LLDPE in Haldia portfolio O19010, O21010, O35042 All Haldia LLDPE grades are butene-based. Octene-specific tear, dart and sealing performance cannot be matched; closest butene grade recommended with the gap quantified.

4.0 No melt blown, PP pipe or PP foam grade in Haldia portfolio AS12000N (melt blown), AER003N (PP-R pipe), J1020FF20 (LDPE foam) No grade in the supplied Haldia range approaches the required rheology (MFR 1200 for melt blown; MFR 0.3 for PP-R pipe) or the branching needed for foam. Marked 'No technically suitable Haldia grade'.

5.0 No HDPE cast film or PP cast/metallised film grade in Haldia portfolio F60080 (HDPE cast film), H070SG (PP cast/metallised film) Haldia film grades are blown (HD T6) or tubular-quenched (F110). Closest grade named with the process and optical gap stated explicitly.

6.0 No fuel-tank / hydrocarbon-contact grade in Haldia portfolio 2002F (HDPE fuel tanks, gas cylinders), O35042 (diesel fuel tanks) B5500 and 73204T carry no fuel-contact, permeation or low-temperature-impact qualification in their TDS. Stated honestly as not substitutable for fuel duty; substitution limited to the secondary general-container applications.

7.0 Haldia has no nucleated PP homopolymer and none above MFR 11 H110MAS (nucleated), AM650N (MFR 65), H200MA (MFR 25), H200MK (MFR 20), H200FG (MFR 20), AS160N (MFR 16), H060FU, H110FG, H110FU M110 (MFR 11) is the highest-flow Haldia PP homopolymer; F135 (MFR 35) is the only fibre/coating homopolymer. Flow gaps are stated in each row. For H110MAS the absence of nucleation (isotropic shrinkage / low warpage) is flagged as unmatched.

8.0 Haldia has no ICP extrusion / blow moulding grade C015EG, H019TG (partly), D350MN All Haldia impact copolymers are injection moulding grades. For C015EG the melt-strength gap is stated; for D350MN no Haldia grade combines high flow with No Break notched Izod, and both alternative routes are set out.

9.0 Correction to a claim carried in the IOCL reference sheet Haldia P5300 The IOCL sheet states P5300 is MRS 11.2 MPa / PE112. The official Haldia TDS states: MRS 10 MPa per ISO 9080, designated PE 100 per ISO 12162. This sheet uses the TDS value (PE100). Verified against the rendered TDS page.

10.0 Properties absent from Reliance TDS Numerous — see the Limitations column of each row Where a property is not published it is written 'Not available in official TDS' rather than estimated. Most common omissions: ESCR (stated qualitatively on many HDPE blow grades), Notched Izod on film/tape grades, Vicat on PP grades, and haze/clarity on grades marketed for clarity.

11.0 Test-basis differences between the two producers All HDPE / LLDPE rows Reliance mechanical properties are on compression moulded specimens per ASTM D4976 (PE) or injection moulded Type 1 per ASTM D4101 (PP). Haldia PE properties are on compression moulded sheet per ASTM D4703. Haldia film data is on 25 micron film (2.5 mm die gap, BUR 2.5); Reliance film data on 40 micron film (0.8 mm die gap, BUR 2). Absolute values are therefore not strictly like-for-like; comparisons are directional.

12.0 Dart impact and tear units All film rows Reliance reports Dart F50 in g/µm and tear in g/µm; Haldia reports both in g/µ. Both are per-unit-thickness figures and are compared as such. Note: Haldia F5400 dart (124 g) is reported in grams on 20 micron film at BUR 4.0 — a different basis — and was not used in a numeric comparison.

13.0 Processing parameters All rows Reliance PE TDS quote a single processing temperature band only. Haldia TDS quote barrel, die, parison/quench/oven and mould-water temperatures separately. Where Haldia gives the fuller set this is noted as an advantage; no Haldia-style parameters were invented for Reliance grades.

14.0 Grade matches that are closest-available rather than equivalent Rows where column L carries a parenthetical qualifier Marked inline, e.g. 'closest available — butene grade', 'closest available — impact copolymer, not homopolymer', 'closest available — significant flow gap', 'film duty only'. 42 of the 56 Haldia grades were used; the 14 unused are close variants of grades already selected.

15.0 Direction of advantage All rows Where Haldia is not objectively better, column N says so explicitly and explains the trade-off rather than asserting superiority. This occurs in roughly one third of rows.
